name: Drug Supply Chain Security Act
owner: US FDA (Title II of the Drug Quality and Security Act)
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit/diverted prescription drugs in the US supply chain
adoption_penetration: US federal mandate covering essentially all human, finished, prescription drugs across the domestic supply chain (manufacturers, repackagers, wholesale distributors, dispensers). Enhanced interoperable, electronic, package-level traceability requirements became effective 27 Nov 2023; FDA issued a one-year stabilization exemption to 27 Nov 2024, with further phased dispenser timelines into 2025 (FDA).
effectiveness_verified: inconclusive: No rigorous peer-reviewed outcome evaluation establishes that serialization/track-and-trace (EU FMD, operational 2019; US DSCSA) has reduced falsified-medicine incidence. WHO reports that substandard/falsified products concentrate in low- and middle-income countries (~1 in 10 medicines) and in informal markets and unauthorized online sales - channels largely outside the regulated supply chains these systems secure - and lists track-and-trace as only one enabling tool among many. Legal-supply-chain baseline incidence in the EU/US was already very low, so a measurable incidence reduction attributable to serialization has not been demonstrated.
source_note: FDA page confirms 2013 enactment and package-level interoperable electronic trace goal phased over ten years.

name: Falsified Medicines Directive
public_harm_addressed: falsified medicines entering the legal supply chain
adoption_penetration: Mandatory across 30 European countries (all EU Member States plus the EEA and Switzerland) operating the verification system it requires; safety features on prescription-medicine packs live since 9 Feb 2019 (EMVO system description, 2019). [https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/59efb019-57a1-4161-99a2-9b5cc63d3d26_en?filename=trends_medicinal-products-falsification_study_en.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: limited - the EU Commission study supporting its report to the European Parliament (2024) concluded 'conclusions can hardly be drawn about its overall effectiveness'; only a handful of falsifications were detected in the legal supply chain (EMA confirmed cases fell from 24 in 2017 to 3 in 2022) and 2023 Q2 decommissioning averaged only 75.4%. [https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/59efb019-57a1-4161-99a2-9b5cc63d3d26_en?filename=trends_medicinal-products-falsification_study_en.pdf]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Directive 2011/62/EU of 8 June 2011 on preventing falsified medicinal products.

name: Delegated Regulation on safety features
public_harm_addressed: verification of medicine authenticity at dispensing
references_builds_on: Commission Delegated Regulation implementing the Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU (defines the unique identifier and anti-tampering device).
adoption_penetration: Applies in the 30 EMVS countries; requires a unique identifier (2D Data Matrix) plus an anti-tampering device on prescription packs from 9 Feb 2019 (Italy and Greece on a six-year extended timeline). [https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/59efb019-57a1-4161-99a2-9b5cc63d3d26_en?filename=trends_medicinal-products-falsification_study_en.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: limited - the same EU Commission 2024 study found the safety-features system detected only a few falsified medicines in the legal supply chain and that overall effectiveness could not be established, partly due to incomplete implementation and low decommissioning rates. [https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/59efb019-57a1-4161-99a2-9b5cc63d3d26_en?filename=trends_medicinal-products-falsification_study_en.pdf]
source_note: EUR-Lex ELI confirms Delegated Reg (EU) 2016/161 detailing the unique identifier and anti-tampering safety features; applied 9 Feb 2019.

name: European Medicines Verification System / Organisation
owner: European Medicines Verification Organisation (industry stakeholder non-profit)
public_harm_addressed: falsified medicines reaching patients
references_builds_on: Legal basis: Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161 on safety features.
adoption_penetration: 30 participating countries; ~2,800 pharmaceutical companies onboarded to the EU Hub and 120,000+ connected end-users (110,000+ pharmacies, 6,000+ hospital pharmacies, 4,000+ wholesalers); operational since 9 Feb 2019 (EMVO 'EMVS Explained'). [https://emvo-medicines.eu/wp-content/uploads/The-European-Medicines-Verification-System-Explained.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: limited - EU Commission 2024 study concluded the system has contributed to detecting only a few falsification cases and that its overall effectiveness could not be demonstrated. [https://emvo-medicines.eu/wp-content/uploads/The-European-Medicines-Verification-System-Explained.pdf]
source_note: EMVO site confirms 2015 founding and operation of the European Hub / EMVS mandated by the FMD.

name: GDSN for Healthcare
public_harm_addressed: inaccurate product master data affecting patient safety
adoption_penetration: Nearly 1 million healthcare items registered in the GDSN (growth driven largely by the US FDA UDI rule); GDSN overall used by 25,000+ companies across more than 150 countries (GS1 UK). [https://www.gs1uk.org/insights/news/gdsn-now-holds-global-data-on-almost-1-million-healthcare-items]
source_note: GS1 healthcare page confirms GDSN shares trusted master product data across partners as a global standard.

name: FDA Unique Device Identification
public_harm_addressed: inability to identify/trace and recall unsafe or counterfeit devices
adoption_penetration: 5,152,799 device identifier records in the GUDID full release dated 3 July 2026 (AccessGUDID/NLM); 7,681 US labelers per FDA GUDID data trends (data current 8 Dec 2025). [https://accessgudid.nlm.nih.gov/download]
source_note: FDA page confirms 2013 final rule, mandatory UDI, GUDID submission, and use of issuing agencies GS1/HIBCC/ICCBBA.

name: EU MDR UDI system / EUDAMED
owner: European Commission and national competent authorities
public_harm_addressed: weak traceability and post-market surveillance of devices
references_builds_on: Implements Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR); operational framework set by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/2078; its UDI model aligns with the IMDRF UDI System Application Guide.
adoption_penetration: The EUDAMED Actor registration, UDI/Device registration, Notified Bodies & Certificates, and Market Surveillance modules become mandatory EU-wide on 28 May 2026 (per the European Commission); two further modules — Post-Market Surveillance/Vigilance and Clinical Investigation/Performance Studies — remain under development with no set mandatory date. [https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-eudamed/overview_en]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2017/745 (5 Apr 2017); Basic UDI-DI/UDI-DI/PI with EUDAMED registration, device module mandatory from 2026.

name: IMDRF UDI System / Application Guide
public_harm_addressed: fragmented, non-interoperable national device identification
references_builds_on: The Application Guide recognizes three accredited UDI issuing agencies as conformant device-identification systems: GS1, HIBCC, and ICCBBA.
adoption_penetration: Founding IMDRF regulatory members (US FDA, EU, Japan's PMDA, Health Canada, Australia's TGA, Brazil's ANVISA, and the Asian Harmonization Working Party) aligned on the UDI approach from the guide's inception; China's regulator joined IMDRF as a full member in March 2013 and adopted the UDI framework. [https://www.raps.org/resource/imdrf-issues-major-guidance-outlining-udi-framewor.html]
source_note: IMDRF working-group listing confirms it issues the harmonized regulator UDI Application Guide.

name: WHO Global Surveillance and Monitoring System
public_harm_addressed: undetected substandard and falsified medical products
adoption_penetration: 1,500 reports of substandard or falsified medical products received since the system was set up in 2013 (WHO, 2017); WHO estimates about 1 in 10 (10.5%) medical products in low- and middle-income countries are substandard or falsified. [https://www.who.int/news/item/28-11-2017-1-in-10-medical-products-in-developing-countries-is-substandard-or-falsified]
source_note: WHO fact sheet confirms GSMS launched 2013 as a reporting portal for national regulators.

name: WHO Member State Mechanism on SF products
public_harm_addressed: lack of coordinated global response to SF medical products
references_builds_on: Complements the WHO Global Surveillance and Monitoring System (GSMS) for substandard/falsified medical products, launched July 2013; WHO estimates at least 1 in 10 medicines in low- and middle-income countries are substandard or falsified, costing an estimated US$30.5 billion/year.
adoption_penetration: As of 2025, 45 of 47 WHO African Region countries have nominated National Focal Points integrated into WHO's surveillance system — up from only 5 countries when the situation was reported to WHO's Executive Board in January 2025 — generating 39 regional alerts between 2020 and 2025. [https://healthpolicy-watch.news/who-delays-falsified-medicine-mechanism-reform-amid-health-crisis/]
effectiveness_verified: mixed — WHO's independent 2024 evaluation of the Member State Mechanism found it remains 'a vital platform' but is hindered by inadequate sustainable funding and inconsistent member-state engagement, per WHO Assistant Director-General Dr Chikwe Ihekweazu. [https://healthpolicy-watch.news/who-delays-falsified-medicine-mechanism-reform-amid-health-crisis/]
source_note: WHO fact sheet confirms a Member State mechanism for collaboration on SF products.

name: Turkey Pharmaceutical Track and Trace System
public_harm_addressed: falsified and reimbursement-fraud medicines
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: Covers effectively the whole retail market - the single-payer SGK reimburses ~95% of pharmaceutical sales; full track-and-trace operational since 2012; pharmacy inspector needs fell from ~3,000 to ~100 after rollout (peer-reviewed GHS:SP evaluation, 2020). [https://www.ghspjournal.org/content/8/3/431]
effectiveness_verified: mixed - the peer-reviewed evaluation (Global Health: Science and Practice, 2020) found reimbursement fraud, previously estimated at ~US$1 billion/year, is now 'highly unlikely,' but the authors state quantitative data on the system's detection of falsified/poor-quality medicines are not available. [https://www.ghspjournal.org/content/8/3/431]
source_note: Peer-reviewed article confirms ITS as the first full pharma track-and-trace, mandatory, MoH-operated, GS1 DataMatrix based.

name: Brazil National Medicines Control System
public_harm_addressed: falsified and diverted medicines in Brazil
references_builds_on: Uses two-dimensional barcode serialization on medicine packaging administered by ANVISA; ANVISA cites alignment with other countries' serialized track-and-trace regimes as a rationale for keeping the model.
adoption_penetration: Established by Law 11.903/2009; implementation deadlines set by Law 13.410/2016 (through 28 April 2022). ANVISA invested R$4.9 million with Hospital das Clínicas/USP and contracted R$47.8 million with Dataprev to build the 2D-barcode serialization system, before a 2022 legislative bill (PL 3.846) moved to revoke mandatory serialization, prompting ANVISA to publicly oppose the rollback. [https://www.gov.br/anvisa/pt-br/assuntos/noticias-anvisa/2022/anvisa-propoe-rediscussao-rastreabilidade]
source_note: ANVISA page confirms SNCM created by Lei 11.903/2009 (amended 13.410/2016), DataMatrix-based tracking.

name: Saudi Arabia SFDA Track-and-Trace
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit/diverted human pharmaceuticals
adoption_penetration: Test version launched 2018; live operation from 2019. 6,000+ stakeholders registered between January 2019 and end-2021; the system covers all human pharmaceutical products manufactured in or imported into Saudi Arabia. [https://www.sfda.gov.sa/en/node/87600]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — SFDA reports over 15 million medication boxes recalled through the system and more than 3 billion operation transactions recorded by end-2021. [https://www.sfda.gov.sa/en/node/87600]
source_note: SFDA page confirms RSD tracks all human pharmaceuticals production-to-consumption on GS1 standards, deployed end-2018.

name: India QR/bar code on notified drug brands
owner: CDSCO, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit/spurious medicines among top brands
references_builds_on: Added as Schedule H2 to the Drugs Rules, 1945 via the Drugs (Eighth Amendment) Rules, 2022; brands identified by the NPPA on the Drugs Technical Advisory Board's recommendation.
adoption_penetration: 300 top-selling drug brands required to carry a bar code or QR code on the primary (or secondary) package label from 1 August 2023 (Union Health Ministry notification). [https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/union-health-ministry-notifies-300-drug-brands-under-schedule-h2-details-102657]
source_note: Regulatory media confirms CDSCO requirement for QR/bar codes on 300 notified drug brands from 1 Aug 2023.

name: China Drug Traceability Code system
public_harm_addressed: falsified and unsafe drugs; recall control
references_builds_on: Jointly administered by NHSA, NMPA, the National Health Commission, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security; uses a 20-digit code applied at large/medium/small packaging levels, intended to prevent counterfeit and diverted ('回流药') drugs.
adoption_penetration: A joint National Healthcare Security Administration (NHSA)/NMPA/health-ministry notice (March 2025) mandated nationwide code collection and scanning by 30 June 2025. In Fujian province alone, over 8.3 billion traceability-code records had been accumulated and 25,371 designated medical institutions integrated with the system by end-June 2025. [https://www.news.cn/politics/20241206/080257c8d0b148788f5d669530fa78c3/c.html]
source_note: Regulatory database confirms the NMPA Identification Specification for Drug Traceability Code (2022).

name: EU Cosmetic Products Notification Portal
public_harm_addressed: unnotified/unsafe cosmetics; poison-centre response
references_builds_on: Implements Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 (EU Cosmetics Regulation) — Article 13 for general product notification and Article 16 for products containing nanomaterials.
adoption_penetration: Use of CPNP has been mandatory EU-wide since 2013 for placing any cosmetic product on the market. [https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/sectors/cosmetics/cosmetic-product-notification-portal_en]
source_note: EC page confirms CPNP as the mandatory notification system under Reg (EC) 1223/2009.

name: Health Industry Bar Code / HIBCC
sector_detail: medical devices and healthcare supply chain
public_harm_addressed: non-standard device/product identification
adoption_penetration: Founded in 1983. HIBCC remains one of only three FDA-accredited UDI issuing agencies for the US medical-device UDI system today, alongside GS1 and ICCBBA, per FDA's current issuing-agency listing. [https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/unique-device-identification-system-udi-system/contact-fda-accredited-issuing-agency]
source_note: HIBCC site confirms it is an accredited healthcare SDO providing UDI-compliant Auto-ID standards and the Health Industry Number.

name: FSMA Section 204 Food Traceability Rule
public_harm_addressed: slow tracing of contaminated food during outbreaks
adoption_penetration: FDA estimates the rule affects approximately 323,000 domestic businesses across roughly 484,100 establishments (about 12,000 farms/aquaculture operations and about 443,000 retail food establishments and restaurants). The compliance deadline was delayed from 20 January 2026 to 20 July 2028, with Congress directing non-enforcement before that date (November 2025). [https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/fsma-final-rule-requirements-additional-traceability-records-certain-foods]
source_note: FDA confirms 2022 rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S), Critical Tracking Events/KDEs; compliance extended to 20 Jul 2028.

name: General Food Law, Article 18 (Traceability)
public_harm_addressed: inability to withdraw/recall unsafe food and feed
adoption_penetration: In force EU-wide since 2002. Article 18 requires that traceability of food, feed, food-producing animals, and any substance intended for incorporation into food or feed 'be established at all stages of production, processing and distribution,' with operators required to identify suppliers and track downstream distribution (Recitals 28-29). [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32002R0178]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EC) 178/2002 (28 Jan 2002); Article 18 one-step-back/one-step-forward traceability.

name: Codex traceability/product tracing principles
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent, trade-restrictive national traceability rules
adoption_penetration: Adopted by the Codex Alimentarius Commission in 2006. [https://www.fao.org/fao-who-codexalimentarius/sh-proxy/tr/?lnk=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fworkspace.fao.org%2Fsites%2Fcodex%2FStandards%2FCXG+60-2006%2FCXG_060e.pdf]
source_note: Confirmed 2006 adoption and voluntary traceability principles within food inspection/certification.

name: Traceability in the feed and food chain
public_harm_addressed: fragmented traceability system design
references_builds_on: Positioned alongside ISO 9001 (Quality Management) and ISO 22000 (Food Safety Management Systems) — organizations pursuing ISO 22000 certification are expected to have a traceability system in place, for which ISO 22005 provides design and implementation guidance.
adoption_penetration: Published by ISO in 2007 and currently listed as an active standard in the ISO catalogue (ISO/TC 34). [https://www.iso.org/standard/36297.html]
source_note: ISO confirms ISO 22005:2007 general principles for feed/food chain traceability system design (confirmed 2022).

name: Global Food Safety Initiative
public_harm_addressed: duplicative audits and inconsistent scheme credibility
adoption_penetration: 13 GFSI-recognised certification programme owners under the Version 2020 Benchmarking Requirements (BRCGS, CanadaGAP, Freshcare, FSSC 22000, Global Red Meat Standard, Global Seafood Alliance, GLOBALG.A.P., GRMA, IFS, Japan Food Safety Management Association, PrimusGFS, SQF). [https://mygfsi.com/how-to-implement/recognition/certification-programme-owners/]
source_note: GFSI (CGF) benchmarks/recognises food safety schemes (once certified, recognised everywhere).

name: BRCGS Global Standard for Food Safety
public_harm_addressed: unsafe manufactured food reaching retail
adoption_penetration: Over 28,000 certificated supplier sites in over 100 countries (BRCGS Directory of certified sites, current). [https://www.brcgs.com/about-brcgs/faqs/specifiers/]
source_note: GFSI CPO listing confirms BRCGS Food Safety (issue 9) as GFSI-recognised; ownership LGC/BRC Trading Ltd.

name: SQF (Safe Quality Food) Program
public_harm_addressed: unverified food safety/quality management
adoption_penetration: 14,000+ certified sites in over 40 countries across 6 continents (SQF Institute, current). [https://www.sqfi.com/our-program/what-is-sqf]
source_note: SQFI confirms administration by SQF Institute (FMI, 2003), GFSI-benchmarked, 13 industry codes.

name: FSSC 22000 Certification Scheme
public_harm_addressed: uncontrolled food safety hazards
adoption_penetration: More than 40,000 organizations FSSC 22000 certified worldwide (Foundation FSSC announcement, 18 December 2025). [https://www.fssc.com/insights/fssc-announces-40000-organizations-fssc-22000-certified/]
source_note: Foundation FSSC confirms an ISO 22000-based food safety management certification scheme, GFSI-recognised (v6).

name: IFS Food Standard
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent supplier food safety for private label
adoption_penetration: Over 30,000 IFS certificates and Letters of Compliance issued (IFS, current). [https://www.ifs-certification.com/en/]
source_note: IFS confirms IFS Food originated 2003 (HDE/FCD), administered by IFS Management GmbH; GFSI-recognised (v8).

name: GLOBALG.A.P. Integrated Farm Assurance
public_harm_addressed: unsafe/irresponsible on-farm production
adoption_penetration: 195,000+ certified producers in 130+ countries; 4.5 million+ hectares of certified plant production annually (GLOBALG.A.P., current figures). [https://globalgap.org/about/]
effectiveness_verified: mixed: Case evidence on GLOBALG.A.P. adoption among Peruvian mango producers (AgEcon Search) finds selective rather than broad inclusion: some smallholders participate through exporter-financed contract farming that covers technical guidance and certification costs, but access is conditional on geographic proximity to the exporter, demonstrated reliability, and short-notice delivery capacity, and participation is often short-lived (up to ~3 years). Consistent with the wider literature, private food-safety standards tend to favor larger or better-connected farmers, with smallholder inclusion depending heavily on intermediary/exporter support - a partial, conditional inclusion outcome rather than uniform exclusion or inclusion.
source_note: GLOBALG.A.P. confirms EurepGAP (1997) renamed 2007; applied in 130+ countries; GFSI-recognised via HPSS.

name: EU Organic Production and Labelling
public_harm_addressed: fraudulent or inconsistent organic claims
adoption_penetration: 16.9 million hectares under organic farming in the EU in 2022, representing 10.5% of total EU agricultural area (Eurostat). [https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-eurostat-news/w/ddn-20240619-3]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2018/848 (30 May 2018) on organic production/labelling, repealing 834/2007.

name: USDA National Organic Program
public_harm_addressed: fraudulent organic claims
adoption_penetration: 45,578 certified organic operations worldwide in 2020, of which 28,454 (more than 62%) in the United States (USDA AMS annual count from the Organic INTEGRITY Database). [https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDAAMS/bulletins/2ba210e]
source_note: USDA/AMS confirms NOP under the Organic Foods Production Act, accredits certifiers, regulates the USDA Organic Seal.

name: EU Geographical Indications (PDO/PGI/TSG)
public_harm_addressed: counterfeiting and misuse of origin-linked names
adoption_penetration: About 3,500 EU geographical indications registered (as of February 2023); EU GI products had a sales value of EUR 74.76 billion in 2017 (European Commission). [https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/media/news/protecting-local-food-and-drinks-3-500-geographical-indications-registered-2023-02-23_lt]
source_note: EC confirms PDO/PGI/TSG and that Reg (EU) 2024/1143 (in force 13 May 2024) unifies GI rules.

name: EU IUU Fishing Regulation
public_harm_addressed: illegally caught fish entering the EU market
adoption_penetration: The EU catch certification scheme has been in force since 2010 under Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008. [https://www.iuuwatch.eu/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Member-States-Write-up-EN-1.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: mixed/limited — a 2022 analysis of official EU Member State implementation data (IUU Watch coalition, including WWF, Oceana and ClientEarth) found inconsistent enforcement: e.g., Spain checked 100% of catch certificates vs. Lithuania only 72% (2019); 12 Member States applied no risk-based approach to imports; and verification requests to non-EU exporting countries declined from 2014/15 to 2018/19 despite persistent IUU risk. [https://www.iuuwatch.eu/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Member-States-Write-up-EN-1.pdf]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Council Reg (EC) 1005/2008 (IUU) with the import catch certification scheme.

name: FAO Agreement on Port State Measures
owner: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN
owner_normalised: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN
public_harm_addressed: IUU-caught fish landed and entering trade
adoption_penetration: 86 Parties to the Agreement, counting the EU as a single Member Organization Party (thereby covering 100+ States) (FAO). [https://www.fao.org/port-state-measures/background/parties-psma/en/]
source_note: FAO confirms PSMA is the first binding international agreement against IUU fishing, in force June 2016.

name: FAO Global Record of Fishing Vessels
owner: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN
owner_normalised: Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN
public_harm_addressed: anonymous/untraceable vessels enabling IUU fishing
adoption_penetration: Close to 12,000 fishing and fishing-related vessels included, with data provided by 66 FAO Members (FAO). [https://www.fao.org/global-record/news-events/detail/en/c/1603118/]
source_note: FAO confirms the Global Record uses IMO Numbers as unique vessel identifiers to combat IUU fishing.

name: GDST Standard for Interoperable Seafood Traceability
public_harm_addressed: fragmented, non-interoperable seafood traceability data
references_builds_on: Built on GS1 standards — GDST 1.1 adopted the GS1 Digital Link protocol for computer-to-computer data exchange, and GDST 1.2 aligned with the updated GS1 EPCIS data standard, moving from XML to JSON-LD.
adoption_penetration: As of April 2024, more than 60 businesses stood publicly committed to implementing GDST's interoperable seafood traceability standard. [https://thegdst.org/tracing-progress-towards-traceability-in-2024/]
source_note: GDST confirms a non-profit common standard for interoperable digital seafood traceability (KDEs/CTEs).

name: MSC Fisheries Standard
public_harm_addressed: overfishing and unsustainable fishing
adoption_penetration: 18.9% of global marine wild catch is MSC certified (20.6% engaged with the program); 592 fisheries certified of 738 engaged, as of 31 March 2025 (MSC Annual Report 2024-25). [https://www.msc.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/about-the-msc/msc-annual-report-2024-2025.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: mixed: MSC-affiliated authors (Frontiers in Marine Science 2022), using the independent RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database (82 MSC vs. 95 non-MSC stocks, 2014-2018), find MSC-targeted stocks had higher relative biomass (median ~1.28-1.38 of B at maximum sustainable yield vs. ~0.80-0.84 for non-MSC) and far fewer overfished stocks (9% vs. 26-33%). This shows MSC-certified stocks are healthier, but the design is associational and confounded by selection (already well-managed fisheries self-select into certification) and by a disclosed certifier-affiliation conflict of interest, so a causal harm-reduction claim is not established.
source_note: MSC confirms the Fisheries Standard (three principles) for sustainable wild-capture fishing.

name: MSC Chain of Custody Standard
public_harm_addressed: mislabeling/substitution of certified seafood
adoption_penetration: 51,260 sites hold MSC Chain of Custody certification and 21,859 MSC-labelled products were available to consumers in 2024-25 (up from 9,359 products in 2014-15) (MSC Annual Report 2024-25). [https://www.msc.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/about-the-msc/msc-annual-report-2024-2025.pdf]
source_note: MSC confirms the CoC standard segregates and correctly labels certified seafood through the chain.

name: ASC Farm Standards and Chain of Custody
public_harm_addressed: environmental and social harms of aquaculture
adoption_penetration: 2,640 ASC-certified farm sites and 120 certified feed mills; ASC-labelled products available to consumers in 121 countries (ASC, current figures). [https://asc-aqua.org/]
source_note: ASC confirms leading farmed-seafood certification plus a Chain of Custody standard; founded 2010.

name: Fairtrade Standards and the FAIRTRADE Mark
public_harm_addressed: unfair prices/conditions for smallholders and workers
adoption_penetration: Approximately 2 million Fairtrade farmers and workers in about 1,900 producer organizations across 70 countries (Fairtrade International). [https://www.fairtrade.net/en/why-fairtrade/impact/key-figures-at-a-glance.html]
source_note: Fairtrade International confirms it sets Fairtrade Standards with independent certification by FLOCERT.

name: Rainforest Alliance 2020 Sustainable Agriculture Standard
public_harm_addressed: deforestation, human rights abuses, unsustainable farming
adoption_penetration: 7.5 million+ farmers and workers on certified farms; 5.7 million+ hectares certified across 62 countries in 2023; 51% of all cocoa and 17% of all coffee produced worldwide is Rainforest Alliance Certified (2023 Annual Report). [https://www.rainforest-alliance.org/annual_report/2023/]
source_note: Rainforest Alliance confirms the 2020 Standard with traceability/transparency; merged with UTZ in 2018.

name: ISO 22000 Food Safety Management Systems
public_harm_addressed: uncontrolled food safety hazards
adoption_penetration: ISO does not publish an ISO 22000 count on its open pages; the ISO Survey certificate count now sits on IAF CertSearch (captcha-gated dataset, not accessible). Best accessible proxy: FSSC 22000, the certification scheme built on ISO 22000, reports 42,349 certified organizations (FSSC, accessed Jul 2026).
source_note: ISO confirms ISO 22000:2018 food safety management system, basis of FSSC 22000.

name: Global Sustainable Seafood Initiative Benchmark
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent credibility of seafood certification schemes
adoption_penetration: 7 certification schemes recognized as aligned with the GSSI Global Benchmark Tool (CSI, Iceland Responsible Fisheries, MSC, MEL-Japan, BAP, GLOBALG.A.P., ASC) (GSSI). [https://ourgssi.org/gssi-recognized-certifcation/]
source_note: GSSI confirms a public-private Global Benchmark Tool (built on FAO Guidelines) recognising seafood schemes.

name: Best Aquaculture Practices Certification
public_harm_addressed: environmental, social and food safety risks in aquaculture
adoption_penetration: 3,959 BAP-certified facilities (processing plants, farms, hatcheries, feed mills) across 43 countries at the end of 2023, an 18% increase over 2022 (Global Seafood Alliance 2023 Annual Report). [https://www.globalseafood.org/blog/2023-annual-report/]
source_note: GSA confirms BAP covers farm/feed/processing and was the first GSSI-recognised aquaculture programme.

name: OECD Due Diligence Guidance (Minerals)
public_harm_addressed: conflict finance and human rights abuse in mineral chains
adoption_penetration: As of 2025, 313 smelters/refiners are assessed as 'conformant' under the Responsible Minerals Assurance Process (RMAP) — up from just 2 facilities in 2010 — including 91 gold and 54 cobalt facilities; RMAP was the first due-diligence scheme recognized by the European Commission as compliant with the EU Conflict Minerals Regulation. [https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/2025-07/RMI%20Overview%20July%202025%20-%20SEMI.pdf]
source_note: OECD legal instrument confirms the five-step guidance, Council Recommendation of 25 May 2011 (gold suppl. 2012).

name: EU Conflict Minerals Regulation
public_harm_addressed: financing of armed conflict via mineral imports
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: 8,286 EU Union importers of tin/tantalum/tungsten/gold (3TG) identified in 2022; only 477 (6%) exceeded the volume thresholds triggering full due-diligence obligations; total EU 3TG imports valued €18.3bn in 2023 (71% gold ores/concentrates by value). Direct imports from conflict-affected/high-risk areas (CAHRAs) were small shares (e.g. 4.83% of gold ores, 1.46% of tin). [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52024DC0415]
effectiveness_verified: limited — European Commission's first mandatory review (COM(2024) 415, June 2024) found 'limited impacts among local stakeholders that could be attributed directly to the Regulation,' with 'generally low' awareness of the Regulation found in field research in DRC and Colombia, only ~2 years after due-diligence obligations began applying (2021). [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52024DC0415]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2017/821 (17 May 2017) on 3TG importer due diligence; obligations from 1 Jan 2021.

name: Dodd-Frank Act Section 1502 (Conflict Minerals)
public_harm_addressed: conflict finance to armed groups in the DRC region
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: In 2023 SEC filings, an estimated 62% of companies that conducted due diligence were ultimately unable to determine whether their conflict minerals originated in covered countries; only ~15% could determine whether minerals benefitted or financed armed groups (GAO, 2024). [https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107018/index.html]
effectiveness_verified: Counterproductive/limited: US GAO (2024, GAO-25-107018) found 'no empirical evidence that the rule has decreased the occurrence or level of violence in the eastern DRC' and concluded the SEC disclosure rule 'has not reduced violence' and 'has not improved peace and security' in the DRC. [https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107018/index.html]
source_note: SEC fact sheet (2012) confirms the rule implements Sec. 1502 with Form SD disclosure and country-of-origin inquiry.

name: Responsible Minerals Assurance Process
public_harm_addressed: conflict-linked/abusive minerals at smelters/refiners
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: 313 conformant smelters & refiners across RMI due-diligence programs (RMI Overview, 2025). [https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/2025-07/RMI%20Overview%20July%202025%20-%20SEMI.pdf]
source_note: RMI confirms RMAP third-party smelter/refiner assessment; first scheme recognised by the EC under the CMR (2025).

name: LBMA Responsible Sourcing / Good Delivery
public_harm_addressed: money laundering and abuse in bullion chains
adoption_penetration: 66 gold refiners on the LBMA Good Delivery List (current list, 2024), all required to adhere to the LBMA Responsible Sourcing Programme. [https://www.lbma.org.uk/good-delivery/gold-current-list]
source_note: LBMA confirms Good Delivery refiners must pass annual OECD-based due diligence audits or be removed.

name: Responsible Jewellery Council Standards
public_harm_addressed: unethical/conflict-linked/non-traceable materials
adoption_penetration: 1,828 members worldwide operating across 71 countries by end of 2023 (up from 14 founding members), per RJC's 2024 Annual Report. [https://jewellerymonthly.co.uk/responsible-jewellery-council-unveils-2024-annual-report/]
source_note: RJC confirms the Code of Practices and Chain of Custody Standard with member third-party audit.

name: Aluminium Stewardship Initiative Standards
public_harm_addressed: environmental and social harms in aluminium
adoption_penetration: 232 certifications issued (165 Performance Standard V2 + 67 Chain of Custody V1) as of 31 December 2022; ~44% year-on-year growth in Performance Standard certifications (ASI). [https://aluminium-stewardship.org/asi-certification-growth-trends]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm: In contrast to the null deforestation result, Zwerts et al. (Nature 2024), a large camera-trap study across logging concessions in western equatorial Africa, finds FSC-certified concessions had ~1.5x higher mammal encounter rates and ~4.5x higher faunal biomass than non-FSC concessions, with the largest gains for big-bodied species (mammals 10-30 kg ~3.5x; >100 kg ~2.7x) and critically endangered species (~2.7x; forest elephants ~2.5x), attributed to better anti-poaching enforcement. Evidence of a real biodiversity co-benefit of certification even where deforestation effects are unproven.
source_note: ASI confirms a Performance Standard and a Chain of Custody Standard across the aluminium value chain.

name: The Copper Mark
public_harm_addressed: ESG harms in metal production
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: Over 25% of global mined copper produced by Copper Mark-awarded sites; 39 sites awarded and 51 participating sites (Copper Mark, March 2023). By July 2024 this reached 100 participating sites, 77 awarded, and more than one-third of the world's mined copper (Copper Mark milestone reported by Global Mining Review). [https://coppermark.org/over-25-of-global-mined-copper-now-produced-by-copper-mark-awarded-sites/]
source_note: Copper Mark confirms site-level assurance via a Risk Readiness Assessment plus OECD-aligned Joint Due Diligence Standard.

name: IRMA Standard for Responsible Mining
public_harm_addressed: environmental and social/human rights harm at mine sites
adoption_penetration: As of March 2024, 82 mining companies engaged representing 104 sites across 30 countries; 61 sites self-assessing; 6 sites had completed an independent IRMA audit (results published for operations in Zimbabwe, Mexico and Chile). [https://responsiblemining.net/2024/03/27/irma-mining-engagement-update-mar-2024/]
source_note: IRMA confirms a 2018 multi-stakeholder mining standard (400+ requirements) with third-party assessment.

name: Kimberley Process Certification Scheme
public_harm_addressed: conflict/blood diamonds financing rebel movements
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: 60 participants representing 86 countries (EU counted as one); participants 'actively prevent 99.8% of the worldwide trade' in conflict rough diamonds (Kimberley Process). [https://www.kimberleyprocess.com/participants]
effectiveness_verified: Limited/counterproductive: Global Witness (a KP co-founder) withdrew from the scheme in 2011, concluding it failed to stop conflict diamonds and had become 'an accomplice to diamond laundering' (see https://www.globalwitness.org/en/archive/global-witness-leaves-kimberley-process-calls-diamond-trade-be-held-accountable/). [https://www.kimberleyprocess.com/participants]
source_note: KP confirms scheme in force 2003, KP certificate required for cross-border rough diamond trade, national-law enforcement.

name: Forest Stewardship Council
public_harm_addressed: unsustainable forestry, deforestation, forced labour
adoption_penetration: 173,870,727 certified hectares; 69,787 Chain of Custody certificates; members in 89 countries (FSC Facts & Figures, current mid-2026). [https://uk.fsc.org/what-is-fsc/facts-and-figures]
effectiveness_verified: Reduced-harm with regional variation: FSC-collated 2024 peer-reviewed studies find FSC certification 'likely reduced deforestation in three regions of the Brazilian Amazon' (Rana et al. 2024) and greater mammal abundance/biodiversity in FSC concessions (Zwerts et al. 2024), though deforestation effects vary by governance context (see https://connect.fsc.org/monitoring-and-evaluation/impact-evaluations). [https://uk.fsc.org/what-is-fsc/facts-and-figures]
source_note: FSC confirms multi-stakeholder governance with third-party certifiers and forest-to-shelf chain of custody.

name: Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification
public_harm_addressed: unsustainable forestry, illegal/non-traceable timber
adoption_penetration: Almost 300 million hectares of PEFC-certified forest; more than 29,800 chain-of-custody certificate holders; 48 endorsed national/regional systems covering 52 countries, with chain-of-custody in 80+ countries (PEFC Facts & Figures). [https://pefc.org/discover-pefc/facts-and-figures]
source_note: PEFC confirms establishment 30 June 1999, endorsing national certification systems with chain-of-custody labelling.

name: EU Timber Regulation
public_harm_addressed: illegally harvested timber on the EU market
references_builds_on: Implements the EU FLEGT (Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade) Action Plan (2003) and underpins FLEGT Voluntary Partnership Agreements; later replaced by the EUDR (2023/1115).
adoption_penetration: By the 2013–2015 evaluation period: 27 of 28 Member States had designated Competent Authorities (Spain the exception), 26 reported check plans in place, 19 had imposed remedial actions/penalties, and 9 Monitoring Organisations were recognised by the Commission. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52016DC0074]
effectiveness_verified: inconclusive — the European Commission's 2016 evaluation (COM(2016) 74 / SWD(2016) 34) stated the evaluation 'could not quantify the impact of the Regulation on the trade in illegal timber' and 'no conclusion could be drawn' on the prohibition's effectiveness, citing insufficient enforcement experience and uneven due-diligence implementation, though it noted the Regulation raised awareness and influenced similar laws in Australia and Switzerland. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52016DC0074]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 995/2010; illegal-timber prohibition and operator due diligence; being replaced by EUDR.

name: EU Deforestation-free Products Regulation
sector_detail: cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soya, wood
public_harm_addressed: deforestation embedded in commodity imports
references_builds_on: Replaces the EU Timber Regulation (995/2010); the Commission's confirmed 2020-cutoff deforestation-free requirement builds on the FLEGT/EUTR due-diligence model.
adoption_penetration: Entered into force June 2023; covers 8 commodities (cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soy, wood, and derived products) per the European Commission's official implementation page. Enforcement/compliance begins 30 December 2026 for large/medium companies (per the Commission's confirmed timeline) and 30 June 2027 for SMEs. [https://green-forum.ec.europa.eu/nature-and-biodiversity/deforestation-regulation-implementation_en]
effectiveness_verified: not yet assessable — compliance deadlines have not yet passed, so no published outcome findings exist yet per the Commission's own implementation page. [https://green-forum.ec.europa.eu/nature-and-biodiversity/deforestation-regulation-implementation_en]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2023/1115 (31 May 2023); due diligence with geolocation traceability; repeals 995/2010.

name: Lacey Act (2008 plant/timber amendment)
public_harm_addressed: trade in illegally harvested plants/timber
references_builds_on: Amends the original Lacey Act of 1900 (16 U.S.C. § 3371 et seq.) to extend its illegal-take/trafficking prohibitions to plants and plant products.
adoption_penetration: Regulates a U.S. market in which illegal wood-product imports were still estimated at $2.8 billion in 2013 despite the amendment; China's sourcing of logs/sawn wood from high-risk countries fell from 80% (2007) to 45% (2013), per the 2015 Forest Trends/WRI assessment cited by the Union of Concerned Scientists. [https://www.srs.fs.usda.gov/news/578]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — USDA Forest Service Southern Research Station research (Jeff Prestemon, published in Forest Policy and Economics, 2014/2015) found prices of lumber/hardwood plywood imports from suspected illegal-wood-source countries rose and quantities fell after the 2008 amendment; a companion trade-data analysis found imports of illegal wood into the U.S. declined by an estimated 32–44% since the amendments took effect, concluding 'the amendment has met at least some of its advocates' objectives.' [https://www.srs.fs.usda.gov/news/578]
source_note: CBP confirms the 2008 amendment extended the Act to plants/timber with an import declaration requirement.

name: ISO 38200 Chain of custody of wood
public_harm_addressed: unverifiable custody/origin claims for wood products
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
source_note: ISO confirms ISO 38200:2018 chain-of-custody control system (reconfirmed 2024).

name: ResponsibleSteel International Standard
public_harm_addressed: high-carbon and socially harmful steel
adoption_penetration: 70 certified sites (22 steelmaking, 4 upstream, 38 downstream) across 14 countries; 150+ member companies; certified sites represent 124 million tonnes ~ 6.4% of global steel production (ResponsibleSteel Progress Report, Feb 2024). [https://responsible-steel.shorthandstories.com/progress-report-2024/index.html]
source_note: ResponsibleSteel confirms a multi-stakeholder Production Standard covering sourcing and production (v2.1.1, 2024).

name: Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative
public_harm_addressed: corruption and opacity in extractive revenues
adoption_penetration: 55 implementing countries; USD 3.3 trillion of revenues reported through the EITI in open format (EITI Progress Report 2025). [https://eiti.org/eiti-progress-report-2025]
effectiveness_verified: Mixed/inconclusive: a CMI review of EITI evaluations (Lujala, Rustad & Le Billon, 2017) found EITI succeeded in institutionalizing transparency as a global norm but that there is 'little evidence that the EITI has contributed to improvement in development outcomes,' with impact on corruption/development remaining an open question (https://www.cmi.no/publications/6300-has-the-eiti-been-successful). [https://eiti.org/eiti-progress-report-2025]
source_note: EITI confirms establishment 2003, multi-stakeholder governance, disclosure of extractive payments/revenues.

name: World Gold Council Responsible Gold Mining Principles
public_harm_addressed: ESG harms in gold mining
adoption_penetration: Conformance with the RGMPs is a membership requirement for all World Gold Council members (29 member companies as of 2024-25); the 33 members with operating mines collectively produce c.1,300 tonnes of gold per year (a majority of large-scale gold production), per WGC (Sept 2023). Members must publicly disclose conformance. [https://www.gold.org/about-us]
source_note: WGC confirms the 2019 RGMP framework with external third-party assurance and public conformance disclosure.

name: ICMM Mining Principles
owner: International Council on Mining and Metals
owner_normalised: International Council on Mining and Metals
public_harm_addressed: ESG and governance harms across member operations
adoption_penetration: 27 corporate members and 47 association members; ICMM members represent about one-third of the global metals and mining industry, and conformance with the Mining Principles is a condition of membership (ICMM). [https://www.icmm.com/en-gb/our-story/our-members]
source_note: ICMM confirms Performance Expectations mandatory for members with three-year third-party site validation.

name: ITSCI Programme (3T minerals)
owner: International Tin Association and T.I.C. (with Pact)
public_harm_addressed: conflict finance and abuse in upstream 3T chains
adoption_penetration: 2,958 monitored mine sites and 88,367 artisanal & small-scale miners; 25,716 tonnes of 3T minerals exported and 654,085 tags used in 2024; supply chains across 45+ countries, with field implementation in Burundi, DRC, Rwanda and Uganda (ITSCI 2024 Annual Review). [https://www.itsci.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ITSCI-2024-Annual-Review_EN.pdf]
source_note: ITSCI confirms a not-for-profit upstream traceability/due-diligence programme in four African countries, OECD-aligned.

name: Fairmined Standard
public_harm_addressed: informal/unsafe ASM practices and market access
adoption_penetration: Since 2014, USD 8 million in Fairmined Premium paid to certified mining organizations; more than 430 businesses in 40 countries work with Fairmined gold; certified artisanal/small-scale mining organizations currently in 2 countries (Colombia and Peru) (Fairmined). [https://fairmined.org/our-impact/]
source_note: Fairmined confirms an ARM-owned standard (v2.0, 2014) for ASM gold with traceability and premiums.

name: Fairtrade Gold Standard
public_harm_addressed: poor conditions/market access for ASM gold miners
adoption_penetration: 1,283 kg of gold exported under Fairtrade terms in 2024; over 6.2 tonnes exported under Fairtrade terms cumulatively over the past 10 years (Fairtrade International). [https://www.fairtrade.net/en/products/Fairtrade_products/gold.html]
source_note: Fairtrade International confirms the Gold and Associated Precious Metals Standard for ASM organisations.

name: FLEGT Licensing Scheme for timber
owner: Council of the EU (VPAs; European Commission)
public_harm_addressed: illegal logging and governance failures
adoption_penetration: Indonesia became the first (and to date only) country to issue FLEGT licences, starting November 2016 (VPA signed 2011); FLEGT IMM surveys of EU importers and Competent Authorities indicate the licensing system 'has worked effectively and efficiently.' [https://flegtimm.eu/country-profiles/indonesia/]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EC) 2173/2005 establishing FLEGT licensing via Voluntary Partnership Agreements.

name: Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation
public_harm_addressed: environmental harm from unsustainable, non-circular products
references_builds_on: Replaces the 2009 Ecodesign Directive (2009/125/EC); establishes the legal basis for the EU Digital Product Passport.
adoption_penetration: Entered into force 18 July 2024, applying to 'nearly all physical goods sold in the EU.' The Commission's first Ecodesign and Digital Product Passport Working Plan 2025–2030 (COM(2025) 187, adopted 16 April 2025) prioritises textiles, furniture, tyres, mattresses, iron & steel, aluminium, and several energy-related products (washing machines, dryers, dishwashers, TVs). EU Central DPP Registry deadline set for 19 July 2026. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ%3AL_202401781]
effectiveness_verified: not yet assessable — sector-specific delegated acts are only expected from early 2027, so no published outcome findings exist yet. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ%3AL_202401781]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2024/1781 (13 Jun 2024) establishing the ecodesign framework and DPP.

name: EU Digital Product Passport
public_harm_addressed: information asymmetry blocking repair, reuse, recycling
references_builds_on: W3C Verifiable Credentials and Decentralized Identifiers
adoption_penetration: Established under ESPR (2024/1781); EU Central DPP Registry deadline 19 July 2026, with first sector-specific delegated acts (textiles, furniture, tyres, mattresses, iron/steel, aluminium, and priority energy-related products) expected from early 2027 per the Commission's 2025–2030 Working Plan (COM(2025) 187, April 2025); batteries subsector registration obligation begins 18 February 2027. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ%3AL_202401781]
effectiveness_verified: not yet assessable — rollout has not yet begun, so no published outcome findings exist yet. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ%3AL_202401781]
source_note: EC confirms the DPP under ESPR, accessed via data carrier; batteries mandatory from 18 Feb 2027.

name: Batteries and Waste Batteries Regulation
object_attributes: composition, sustainability-carbon, origin-provenance, chain-of-custody, safety, compliance-conformity
public_harm_addressed: environmental and social harms across the battery lifecycle
references_builds_on: Repeals Directive 2006/66/EC (the earlier EU Batteries Directive).
adoption_penetration: Entered into force 17 August 2023 with a phased compliance schedule: safety/performance requirements from 18 Aug 2024; carbon-footprint declarations for EV batteries from 18 Feb 2025; supply-chain due-diligence and waste-management obligations from 18 Aug 2025; carbon-footprint requirements for industrial batteries from 18 Feb 2026; battery passports and removability/replaceability rules from 18 Feb 2027; recycled-content requirements from 18 Aug 2028. Applies to 5 battery categories (portable, SLI, light-transport, industrial, EV). [https://www.tuv.com/landingpage/en/eu-new-battery-regulation-eu-2023-1542/]
effectiveness_verified: not yet assessable — the phased compliance schedule runs through 2028, so no published outcome findings exist yet. [https://www.tuv.com/landingpage/en/eu-new-battery-regulation-eu-2023-1542/]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2023/1542 (12 Jul 2023), in force 17 Aug 2023, repealing Dir 2006/66/EC.

name: EU Battery Passport
public_harm_addressed: unverifiable lifecycle/material data hindering circularity
references_builds_on: Implements Article 77 and Annex XIII of the Batteries and Waste Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.
adoption_penetration: Mandatory from 18 February 2027 for EV, light-means-of-transport, and industrial batteries with capacity >2 kWh (per Battery Regulation Annex XIII). A proof-of-concept pilot launched 18 January 2023 at WEF Davos under the Global Battery Alliance, with Audi (VW Group) and Tesla publicly demonstrating passports and founding members including BASF, CATL, Eurasian Resources Group, Glencore, LG Energy Solution, and Umicore. [https://www.globalbattery.org/press-releases/global-battery-alliance-launches-world%E2%80%99s-first-battery-passport-proof-of-concept/]
effectiveness_verified: inconclusive — the GBA pilot disclosed that 'the quality of the data presented in the proof-of-concept battery passports has not been fully verified and was partially complemented with reasonable data estimates,' covering only select raw-material supply chains rather than full battery inputs. [https://www.globalbattery.org/press-releases/global-battery-alliance-launches-world%E2%80%99s-first-battery-passport-proof-of-concept/]
source_note: EC confirms the battery passport becomes mandatory 18 Feb 2027 as the first DPP application.

name: Global Battery Alliance Battery Passport
public_harm_addressed: unverified ESG performance in battery chains
adoption_penetration: The world-first Battery Passport proof of concept was launched January 2023 at the World Economic Forum in Davos; prototype passports were piloted and publicly shared by Audi (Volkswagen AG) and Tesla, with the framework developed collaboratively by 130+ organizations across the battery value chain (miners, cell makers, recyclers, NGOs, governments). [https://www.globalbattery.org/press-releases/global-battery-alliance-launches-world%E2%80%99s-first-battery-passport-proof-of-concept/]
source_note: GBA confirms the Battery Passport proof of concept (Davos 2023) with a certification scheme targeted for 2027.

name: UN/CEFACT Recommendation 46 (garment/footwear traceability)
public_harm_addressed: supply-chain opacity enabling unethical production
references_builds_on: Part of UN/CEFACT's broader traceability and transparency recommendations framework for sustainable value chains.
adoption_penetration: As of February 2024, the UNECE Sustainability Pledge (the implementation vehicle for Rec 46's traceability/transparency framework) had 105 pledges from 97 actors across 27 countries and 5 continents, with 800+ partners involved; Europe accounted for 55.6% of pledging organisations. [https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2024-06/SustainabilityPledge-3yrsMonitoringReport_0.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: mixed — UNECE's 3-year monitoring report (June 2024) found 84% of surveyed pledgers (62 pledges monitored Feb–May 2024) reported being 'on track' with objectives, but only 16% added new KPIs after initial disclosure (66% disclosed KPIs initially), indicating limited evolution in measurement rigor. [https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2024-06/SustainabilityPledge-3yrsMonitoringReport_0.pdf]
source_note: UNECE confirms Rec 46 (ECE/TRADE/463) adopted at the 27th UN/CEFACT Plenary, Feb 2021.

name: Textile Exchange Content Claim Standard
public_harm_addressed: unverifiable raw-material content claims
references_builds_on: Requires certification bodies to hold ISO/IEC 17065:2012 accreditation ('Conformity assessment — Requirements for bodies certifying products, processes and services') 'at the same time as or prior to' obtaining accreditation to any Textile Exchange standard, per Textile Exchange's own Accreditation and Certification Procedures (ASR-101 V2.1).
adoption_penetration: No verified certified-site/facility adoption figures were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://textileexchange.org/app/uploads/2021/02/ASR-101-V2.1-Accreditation-Certification-Procedures-for-Textile-Exchange-Standards.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: No verified published effectiveness/outcome findings were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://textileexchange.org/app/uploads/2021/02/ASR-101-V2.1-Accreditation-Certification-Procedures-for-Textile-Exchange-Standards.pdf]
source_note: Textile Exchange confirms the CCS as its foundational chain-of-custody standard for input claims.

name: Global Recycled Standard
public_harm_addressed: false recycled-content claims
references_builds_on: GRS certification bodies operate under ISO/IEC 17065 (product certification) and ISO/IEC 17011 (accreditation), and the standard references EU REACH (Reg. (EC) No 1907/2006) — Article 57 / Annex XIV substances of very high concern — for chemical restrictions.
adoption_penetration: Over 10,000 active GRS certificates reported (Textile Exchange GRS factsheet compiled by the EU Sustcert4Biobased project, 2024). [https://sustcert4biobased.eu/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Textile-Exchange-GRS_factsheet.pdf]
source_note: Textile Exchange confirms GRS verifies recycled content plus processing conditions (with RCS/OCS siblings).

name: Leather Working Group Certification
public_harm_addressed: environmental harm and untraceable leather sourcing
adoption_penetration: Over 2,000 LWG-certified suppliers were engaged globally in 2024, with 600+ brand partners and operations in more than 60 countries; LWG passed the 1,000-certified-manufacturer milestone in 2022. [https://www.leatherworkinggroup.com/learn-more/features/2024-highlights-leather-working-group/]
source_note: LWG confirms audit standards (launched 2005) covering environmental performance and traceability.

name: ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List
public_harm_addressed: discharge of hazardous chemicals into water/products
adoption_penetration: The ZDHC Gateway (described by ZDHC as the world's largest database of safer chemical products for the fashion industry) had 8,741 suppliers enrolled and 17,360 Performance InCheck reports created by 2022; as of December 2023 ZDHC counted 58 chemical-formulator signatories, 41 brand/retailer signatories and 46 supplier signatories. In 2022, 98% of published Gateway wastewater test reports met ZDHC MRSL guidelines. [https://www.roadmaptozero.com/impact-report-2023]
source_note: ZDHC confirms a multi-stakeholder initiative and MRSL managing input chemistry.

name: OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100
public_harm_addressed: harmful substances in textiles reaching consumers
adoption_penetration: Over 25,000 STANDARD 100 certificates were issued in financial year 2021/22 (the first time that threshold was passed), part of 36,084 total OEKO-TEX certificates/labels that year (+14% vs. 31,696 the prior year). Across all OEKO-TEX standards, 50,000+ valid certifications were reached in FY 2023/24 (+22%), with more than 35,000 textile and leather companies relying on them. [https://www.oeko-tex.com/en/news/press-releases/oeko-texr-annual-report-2021-2022]
source_note: OEKO-TEX confirms STANDARD 100 tests components against 1,000+ harmful substances; 1992 origin.

name: Catena-X Automotive Network
public_harm_addressed: fragmented, non-sovereign supply-chain data
references_builds_on: W3C Verifiable Credentials and Decentralized Identifiers
adoption_penetration: Approximately 200+ member organizations are listed in the Catena-X Automotive Network e.V. member roster (dated March 2025), spanning OEMs, tier suppliers, technology and consulting firms, research institutes and industry associations. [https://catena-x.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Catena-X_List-of-Members.pdf]
source_note: Catena-X confirms an open automotive data ecosystem developing standards/certification with global hubs.

name: AS9100 Aerospace Quality Management
public_harm_addressed: unsafe or nonconforming aerospace parts
adoption_penetration: Per the IAQG OASIS supplier directory (as compiled May 2025), there were 10,592 AS9100-certified sites in the United States and 29,224 total aerospace certifications worldwide across AS9100/AS9110/AS9120 combined, up ~18% since April 2023. [https://www.simpleque.com/2025-review-of-as9100-as9110-and-as9120-certifications-worldwide/]
source_note: Accredited body (NQA) confirms AS9100 is an ISO 9001-based aerospace QMS prepared by IAQG/SAE.

name: AS5553 Counterfeit Electronic Parts
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit electronic parts in safety-critical systems
references_builds_on: No verified reference/foundational-standard relationship was found from an authoritative primary source.
adoption_penetration: Originally published 2009, now in its 5th revision (AS5553E, 2025). DoD counterfeit-part detection/avoidance requirements were mandated government-wide via DFARS 252.246-7007 (effective 6 May 2014, implementing Section 818 of the FY2012 NDAA, Pub. L. 112-81, as amended by Section 833 of the FY2013 NDAA). The Federal Register final rule explicitly states DoD 'concurs that industry consensus standards could be used' for compliance but 'has not mandated the use of specific industry standards,' leaving AS5553 as an accepted (not required) compliance route. [https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2014/05/06/2014-10326/defense-federal-acquisition-regulation-supplement-detection-and-avoidance-of-counterfeit-electronic]
effectiveness_verified: No verified published effectiveness/outcome findings were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2014/05/06/2014-10326/defense-federal-acquisition-regulation-supplement-detection-and-avoidance-of-counterfeit-electronic]
source_note: SAE confirms AS5553 (2 Apr 2009) on counterfeit-part avoidance/detection/mitigation/disposition; referenced in US DFARS.

name: AS6081 Counterfeit Parts (Distributors)
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit parts via open-market distribution
references_builds_on: Positioned as complementary to AS5553 — AS5553 targets EEE product designers/manufacturers while AS6081 targets independent distributors; certification bodies must hold ISO 9001 (with AS9120/ISO 13485 as alternatives) before pursuing AS6081 accreditation. Current version AS6081A (2023).
adoption_penetration: No verified adoption/scale figures were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://blog.ansi.org/anab/what-is-as6081/]
effectiveness_verified: No verified published effectiveness/outcome findings were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://blog.ansi.org/anab/what-is-as6081/]
source_note: Accredited body (NQA) confirms AS6081 for distributor counterfeit detection/mitigation, building on AS9120.

name: IDEA-STD-1010 Component Acceptability
public_harm_addressed: substandard/counterfeit components in supply chains
references_builds_on: No verified reference/foundational-standard relationship was found from an authoritative primary source.
adoption_penetration: Standard (rev. 1010-A) introduced October 2006; by August 2007, the Independent Distributors of Electronics Association (IDEA) reported 'more than half of its 38 members' were compliant, and OEMs/CEMs/EMS providers began requiring conformance for approved-vendor-list status. [https://www.eetimes.com/independent-distributors-embrace-component-inspection-standard-readies-certification-program/]
effectiveness_verified: No verified published effectiveness/outcome findings were found from an authoritative primary source. [https://www.eetimes.com/independent-distributors-embrace-component-inspection-standard-readies-certification-program/]
source_note: IDEA confirms IDEA-STD-1010 (Rev B) visual-inspection standard to detect counterfeit components.

name: Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS 2)
public_harm_addressed: hazardous substances in electronics harming health/environment
references_builds_on: RoHS 2 (Directive 2011/65/EU) is the recast of the original RoHS Directive 2002/95/EC.
adoption_penetration: All 27 Member States transposed the Directive by the 2 January 2013 deadline. A 2017 impact-assessment study estimated 23–28% of EEE products did not comply with RoHS; RoHS AdCo joint market-surveillance projects found 24% of 157 USB cables tested (2016) and 25% of LED lamps/batteries tested (2019) exceeded permitted substance concentrations. By December 2022, 80 Commission delegated directives had amended the Directive and over 60 exemption-renewal requests were pending. [https://environment.ec.europa.eu/document/download/e3e74225-d4a0-4e69-966a-6ed3fdb906b0_en?filename=SWD_2023_760_1_EN_autre_document_travail_service_part1_v4.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — the European Commission's evaluation (SWD(2023) 760 final, 7 December 2023) concluded RoHS 'achieved its primary objective of restricting and thereby reducing the use of certain hazardous substances in EEE,' finding restricted substances (cadmium, lead, mercury) in EEE were 'reduced by around two thirds' between 2003 and 2016. [https://environment.ec.europa.eu/document/download/e3e74225-d4a0-4e69-966a-6ed3fdb906b0_en?filename=SWD_2023_760_1_EN_autre_document_travail_service_part1_v4.pdf]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS 2), 8 Jun 2011, restricting hazardous substances in EEE.

name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive
public_harm_addressed: e-waste pollution and lost recoverable resources
adoption_penetration: The EU27 WEEE separate-collection rate was 45.9% in 2020 (46.8% in 2018, 48.3% in 2019), up from 37% in 2011. [https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/circularity/thematic-metrics/materialsandwaste/waste-electrical-and-electronic-equipment-weee-collection-rate]
effectiveness_verified: limited: The 2020 EU27 collection rate of 45.9% fell well short of the Directive's 65% target, with only Bulgaria, Croatia and Finland meeting the target, as electrical equipment placed on the market grew faster than collection. [https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/circularity/thematic-metrics/materialsandwaste/waste-electrical-and-electronic-equipment-weee-collection-rate]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Directive 2012/19/EU on WEEE (recast), 4 Jul 2012.

name: Aura Blockchain Consortium
public_harm_addressed: counterfeiting and provenance opacity in luxury
adoption_penetration: Over 50 million luxury products registered on the Aura Blockchain and more than 50 participating luxury brands, announced September 2024 (consortium founded by LVMH, Prada Group and Cartier/Richemont). [https://auraconsortium.com/news/blockchain-aura-surpasses-50-million-products]
source_note: Aura confirms a non-profit, blockchain-agnostic consortium (LVMH, Prada, Cartier/Richemont, OTB) for luxury product passports.

name: General Product Safety Regulation
public_harm_addressed: unsafe consumer products, including online-sold goods
references_builds_on: Repeals Directive 2001/95/EC (General Product Safety Directive) and Council Directive 87/357/EEC; amends Regulation (EU) 1025/2012 and Directive (EU) 2020/1828.
adoption_penetration: Applies EU-wide from 13 December 2024, replacing the General Product Safety Directive across the single market (EUR-Lex OJ metadata: first date of entry into force/application 2024-12-13). [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/988/oj/eng]
effectiveness_verified: Too recently applicable for published outcome/impact findings as of mid-2026; none located. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/988/oj/eng]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR); application from 13 Dec 2024.

name: Construction Products Regulation (recast)
public_harm_addressed: unsafe/non-performing construction products; missing environmental data
references_builds_on: Repeals and replaces Regulation (EU) No 305/2011, the original Construction Products Regulation.
adoption_penetration: EUR-Lex OJ metadata lists 8 January 2027 as the (phased) date of application/entry into force of the recast. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3110/oj/eng]
effectiveness_verified: Too new (not yet fully applicable) for published outcome data; none located. [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3110/oj/eng]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2024/3110 (27 Nov 2024) repealing 305/2011 and introducing a construction DPP.

name: EN 15804 (Construction EPD core rules)
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent, non-comparable environmental claims
adoption_penetration: The International EPD System (EPD International / Environdec) alone held more than 3,600 valid published EPDs as of October 2022, with 1,000+ registered in 2022 and the construction/buildings sector (governed by EN 15804) showing the strongest growth. [https://environdec.com/news/significant-increase-in-registered-epds]
source_note: International EPD System confirms EN 15804:2012+A2:2019 core PCR for construction-product EPDs.

name: CE Marking (New Legislative Framework)
public_harm_addressed: unsafe/non-compliant products on the single market
adoption_penetration: Covers 30+ EU product-sector harmonisation directives/regulations (electrical equipment, machinery, medical devices, toys, radio equipment, pressure equipment, lifts, PPE, etc.), per the European Commission's 2022 'Blue Guide' on implementation of EU product rules. [https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/european-standards/harmonised-standards/new-legislative-framework-and-eco-management-audit-scheme_en]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EC) 765/2008 setting accreditation/market-surveillance/CE marking principles (Art 30).

name: Toy Safety Regulation
public_harm_addressed: unsafe toys (chemical, physical, digital) reaching children
adoption_penetration: Enters into force 1 January 2026; becomes applicable 1 August 2030 (consistent reporting from Eurofins and UL Solutions based on the EU Official Journal text). [https://www.eurofins.com/toys-hardlines/resources/articles/a-quick-overview-of-the-new-eu-toy-safety-regulation-eu-20252509/]
effectiveness_verified: Not yet applicable; no published outcome data. [https://www.eurofins.com/toys-hardlines/resources/articles/a-quick-overview-of-the-new-eu-toy-safety-regulation-eu-20252509/]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms Reg (EU) 2025/2509 on toy safety (26 Nov 2025), repealing Dir 2009/48/EC, adding a DPP.

name: Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products
public_harm_addressed: illicit tobacco trade and lost excise revenue
references_builds_on: Builds on the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC), specifically Article 15 on eliminating illicit trade in tobacco products.
adoption_penetration: At least 69 Parties bound by the Protocol as of the 2025 reporting cycle, of which 46 (67%) submitted implementation reports (WHO FCTC 2025 Global Progress Report). [https://fctc.who.int/docs/librariesprovider12/meeting-reports/2025-global-progress-report-2025-protocol.pdf?sfvrsn=68325c4e_4&download=true]
source_note: WHO confirms adoption 2013, entry into force 25 Sep 2018, and Article 8 global track-and-trace regime.

name: EU Tobacco Track and Trace (TPD Arts 15-16)
owner: European Commission (DG SANTE); Member State ID issuers
public_harm_addressed: tobacco smuggling and counterfeiting
references_builds_on: TPD Directive 2014/40/EU, Articles 15-16; intended to align with the FCTC Illicit Trade Protocol, Article 8.
adoption_penetration: Unique identifiers mandatory on all cigarette and roll-your-own tobacco packs placed on the EU market since 20 May 2019, extended to all other tobacco products from 20 May 2024. [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7799412]
effectiveness_verified: counterproductive - Peer-reviewed analysis (Gallagher et al., Tobacco Control; PMC7799412) found the EU system compromised by tobacco-industry influence: 7 of 8 approved data repositories had pre-existing ties to major tobacco firms and industry/Inexto retained financial-operational links, concluding the system may not meet Illicit Trade Protocol Article 8 independence requirements and undermines its public-health purpose. [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7799412]
source_note: EC confirms unique-identifier marking and security features, operational 20 May 2019 (cigarettes/RYO).

name: Excisable Goods Management System (Kenya)
public_harm_addressed: excise tax evasion and counterfeit goods
adoption_penetration: Digital excise tax-stamp/track-and-trace system implemented for cigarettes and cigars in Kenya starting November 2013 (peer-reviewed interrupted-time-series study). [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36587853/]
effectiveness_verified: Mixed - the study found the post-implementation slope (trend) of real excise-tax revenue rose significantly, but there was no statistically significant immediate level jump at rollout, indicating gains materialized gradually rather than instantly and depended on sustained compliance effort. [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36587853/]
source_note: KRA confirms a physical excise-stamp track-and-trace system; beverages phase from 1 Sep 2019.

name: SICPATRACE (secure track and trace)
public_harm_addressed: excise fraud, smuggling, counterfeiting
adoption_penetration: 465 billion products marked by SICPATRACE worldwide; e.g., 2.6 billion secured products per year in Brazil (vendor-reported, SICPA facts and figures, 2025). [https://www.sicpa.com/revenue-mobilisation-and-conformity/sicpatrace-evo/facts-and-figures]
source_note: SICPA confirms SICPATRACE serialized marking/track-and-trace/authentication deployed in 20+ countries.

name: Authentix authentication and tax stamp programs
public_harm_addressed: fuel adulteration and excise/tax fraud
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm - Following the launch of Authentix's Track & Trace system in Pakistan (July 2021), tobacco tax collection rose 26% (an increase of ~Rs 21 billion) in the subsequent fiscal half-year (reported Jan 2023), indicating reduced evasion / higher tax capture (vendor report citing national tax-authority data). [https://authentix.com/knowledge-center/tax-collection-from-pakistan-tobacco-industry-increases-significantly/]
source_note: Authentix confirms national digital tax-stamp, fuel-marking and track-and-trace programs for governments.

name: REACH (chemicals regulation)
public_harm_addressed: health/environmental harm from hazardous chemicals
references_builds_on: REACH entered into force in 2007, replacing the EU's former legislative framework for chemicals (European Commission).
adoption_penetration: More than 22,000 substances manufactured/used in the EU had been registered under the REACH procedure as of June 2019 (European Commission). [https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/news/chemicals-european-commission-and-echa-scrutinise-all-reach-registrations-2027-2019-06-25_en]
effectiveness_verified: mixed - The European Commission's second REACH Review (2018, REFIT Scoreboard) concluded the Regulation is 'fundamentally sound' and 'well tuned to addressing the needs and achieving the objectives pursued', while identifying areas needing improvement (registration data gaps, authorisation simplification, level playing field on imports, legislative coherence). [https://op.europa.eu/webpub/com/refit-scoreboard/en/policy/7/7-10.html]
source_note: EC confirms registration duty, SVHC candidate list, authorisation/restriction; entry into force 2007, ECHA-run.

name: SCIP Database (SVHCs in articles)
public_harm_addressed: hidden hazardous substances through to waste stage
references_builds_on: Notification obligation established under the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC).
adoption_penetration: Approximately 14.4 million SCIP notifications of articles containing Substances of Very High Concern held in the ECHA database (live count, 2026). [https://echa.europa.eu/scip-database]
source_note: ECHA confirms SVHC-above-0.1% notification for articles under the Waste Framework Directive from Jan 2021.

name: Globally Harmonized System (UN GHS)
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent chemical hazard communication
references_builds_on: Originates from Chapter 19 of Agenda 21 (Rio Earth Summit, 1992); first UN-endorsed version 2003 (the 'Purple Book').
adoption_penetration: Over 60 countries have implemented the GHS, partly or entirely (UNITAR). [https://unitar.org/sustainable-development-goals/planet/our-portfolio/globally-harmonized-system-classification-and-labelling-chemicals]
source_note: Confirmed the Purple Book is a non-binding UN recommendation harmonizing hazard classification/labels/SDS (UNECE owner; iso/unece pages 403).

name: Verified Carbon Standard
public_harm_addressed: unverified or non-additional carbon offset claims
adoption_penetration: The VCS Program has issued over 1.3 billion carbon credits, representing more than 1 billion tonnes of GHG emissions reduced or removed; Verra programs span 4,254+ active projects across 134 countries (Verra, 2024). [https://verra.org/about/overview/]
source_note: Verra confirms VCS certifies GHG reductions/removals and issues tradeable VCUs (2,500+ projects).

name: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
public_harm_addressed: low-integrity carbon offsets lacking safeguards
adoption_penetration: Gold Standard-certified projects issued 84 million carbon credits in 2024 (up 35% from 2023) and retired 35 million; portfolio of 3,848 projects across 110 countries (Gold Standard Annual Report 2024). [https://www.goldstandard.org/publications/annual-report-2024]
source_note: Gold Standard confirms a non-profit body (founded 2003 by WWF and others) certifying climate/development projects.

name: Core Carbon Principles
owner: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
owner_normalised: Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market
public_harm_addressed: fragmented, low-integrity carbon credits
adoption_penetration: ICVCM approved its first CCP-labelled carbon credits in June 2024: approximately 27 million credits across 7 methodologies (ozone-depleting-substance destruction ~12M; landfill gas ~15M), covering CCP-eligible programs ACR, CAR, Gold Standard and Verra. [https://icvcm.org/integrity-council-announces-first-high-integrity-ccp-labelled-carbon-credits-as-assessments-continue/]
source_note: ICVCM confirms ten science-based CCPs and a CCP label assessing crediting programs for quality.

name: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
public_harm_addressed: carbon leakage from carbon-intensive imports
references_builds_on: Designed to mirror the carbon cost faced by EU producers under the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS); expected to eventually cover over 50% of emissions in ETS-covered sectors (European Commission).
adoption_penetration: Covers 6 sectors (cement, iron & steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen); transitional reporting-only period ran 1 October 2023-31 December 2025, with the definitive (financial-obligation) regime starting 1 January 2026 (European Commission). [https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en]
effectiveness_verified: European Commission review report (COM(2025) 783, 16 Dec 2025) on the transitional period exists but its detailed findings could not be retrieved this session (403 on direct PDF fetch), so no verdict is reported here. [https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en]
source_note: EC confirms transitional reporting Oct 2023 and definitive CBAM certificates from 1 Jan 2026.

name: EU Emissions Trading System
public_harm_addressed: uncapped industrial greenhouse-gas emissions
adoption_penetration: Covers reporting stationary installations and aircraft operators, with maritime shipping joining the system for the first time in 2024 (European Commission).
