[https://climate.ec.europa.eu/news-your-voice/news/eu-emissions-trading-system-has-reduced-emissions-sectors-covered-50-2005-2025-04-04_en]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm - European Commission (April 2025): ETS emissions are now around 50% below 2005 levels in the sectors covered and on track to achieve the 2030 target of -62% (2024 emissions fell ~5% vs 2023). [https://climate.ec.europa.eu/news-your-voice/news/eu-emissions-trading-system-has-reduced-emissions-sectors-covered-50-2005-2025-04-04_en]
source_note: EUR-Lex confirms cap-and-trade for tradeable EU Allowances under Dir 2003/87/EC, launched 2005.

name: CORSIA (aviation carbon offsetting)
public_harm_addressed: growth in international-aviation CO2 emissions
adoption_penetration: 126 states volunteered to participate from the start of CORSIA's first phase (2024-2026), rising to ~130 by January 2026 (IATA); airlines' 2024 offsetting requirement is approximately 55.6 MtCO2 based on ICAO's official 2024 sector growth factor (0.154). [https://www.iata.org/en/programs/sustainability/corsia/]
source_note: ICAO confirms CORSIA adopted 2016; pilot from 2021; mandatory second phase from 2027.

name: ISO 14067 Carbon footprint of products
public_harm_addressed: inconsistent product carbon-footprint quantification
references_builds_on: Builds on ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 (life-cycle-assessment principles/requirements) and references ISO 14025 (Type III environmental declarations).
adoption_penetration: Published as ISO 14067:2018 (1st edition); as of late 2024 it was under systematic review for a new edition (ISO). [https://www.iso.org/standard/71206.html]
source_note: ISO confirms ISO 14067:2018 principles/requirements for quantifying product carbon footprint.

name: EU Product/Organisation Environmental Footprint
public_harm_addressed: unreliable/greenwashed environmental claims
references_builds_on: The PEF/PEFCR methodology is built on the ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 life-cycle-assessment standards (European Commission Joint Research Centre, PEFCR Guidance).
adoption_penetration: European Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 on the use of Environmental Footprint methods to measure and communicate the life-cycle environmental performance of products and organisations (EUR-Lex). [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reco/2021/2279/oj/eng]
source_note: EC confirms the PEF/OEF life-cycle methods (Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279) and PEFCRs.

name: Guarantees of Origin (renewable energy)
owner: EU Member States; Association of Issuing Bodies
owner_normalised: EU Member States; Association of Issuing Bodies
public_harm_addressed: unverifiable renewable-electricity origin claims
adoption_penetration: AIB passed the threshold of 10,000 TWh of cumulative EECS Guarantees of Origin issued by 2025; in 2025 alone over 1,094 TWh were issued and over 978 TWh cancelled (Association of Issuing Bodies). [https://www.aib-net.org/]
source_note: AIB confirms GO legal basis in RED 2018/2001 with EECS cross-border issuing/tracking infrastructure.

name: International REC Standard
public_harm_addressed: lack of trusted renewable-attribute tracking in emerging markets
adoption_penetration: 188 million I-REC(E) certificates (188 TWh of electricity) issued across all I-REC(E) markets in the first half of 2024 (+17% vs H1 2023); 162 million certificates redeemed (I-TRACK Foundation). [https://www.trackingstandard.org/i-rece-market-statistics-for-first-half-of-2024/]
source_note: I-TRACK Foundation confirms the I-REC(E) attribute certificate across 70+ countries with accredited issuers.

name: Green-e Energy certification
public_harm_addressed: unverified voluntary renewable-electricity claims
adoption_penetration: Green-e Energy certified 125.5 million MWh of retail renewable energy transactions in 2023 (highest to date), representing over 3.2% of total U.S. retail electricity use (Center for Resource Solutions verification report). [https://resource-solutions.org/g2024/]
source_note: CRS confirms Green-e Energy certifies voluntary-market renewable electricity and RECs in North America.

name: Renewable Identification Numbers (RFS)
public_harm_addressed: verifying renewable-fuel volumes; preventing blending fraud
adoption_penetration: 25.22 billion RINs were generated under the RFS in 2024, up from 23.85 billion in 2023 (US EPA data, released 17 January 2025). [https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-19-47]
effectiveness_verified: Limited - the US Government Accountability Office found 'the RFS has likely had a limited effect, if any, on greenhouse gas emissions' to date and judged it 'unlikely to meet the greenhouse gas emissions reduction goals envisioned for the program through 2022,' largely because the program has relied on corn-starch ethanol rather than the advanced biofuels needed for substantial reductions. [https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-19-47]
source_note: EPA confirms RINs are the tradeable compliance currency of the RFS, tracked in EPA's EMTS.

name: ISO/IEC 15459 Unique identification
public_harm_addressed: misidentification of items and transport units
adoption_penetration: ISO/IEC 15459 is the umbrella unique-identification framework operated via registered Issuing Agencies; AIM (aimglobal.org) is its Registration Authority and issues/maintains the Issuing Agency Codes. Registered issuing agencies include GS1 and the MA system. Per the MA Identification System White Paper (MA标识代码管理委员会, 2021), the MA agency (authorized as an ISO/IEC 15459 issuing agency in Aug 2018) alone reports 500,000+ registered organizations and 21+ billion identifiers issued/managed as of 2021 — evidencing the framework's operational scale through its issuing agencies. [https://www.aimglobal.org/registration-authority-iso-iec-15459/]
source_note: AIM Global confirms it is the ISO/IEC 15459 Registration Authority; standard covers unique identification of items/units.

name: GS1 General Specifications (GTIN, GLN, SSCC keys)
public_harm_addressed: product misidentification across supply chains
adoption_penetration: GS1 barcodes (carrying GS1 keys such as GTIN) are used to identify over 1 billion products and are scanned more than 10 billion times daily worldwide (GS1 US, 50-year 'scanniversary', June 2024). GS1 separately reports the barcode is used by over 2 million manufacturers on more than 4 trillion product items per year. [https://www.gs1us.org/industries-and-insights/media-center/press-releases/gs1-us-celebrates-50-year-barcode-scanniversary]
source_note: GS1 confirms the General Specifications define GTIN/GLN/SSCC keys and data carriers (Release 26.0, Jan 2026).

name: GS1 Digital Link
public_harm_addressed: fragmented product data behind a scanned identifier
adoption_penetration: Standard ratified 14 August 2018 (official GS1/GS1 US announcement); the industry is now converging on the 'Sunrise 2027' target date for retail point-of-sale scanning of GS1 2D/Digital Link barcodes (GS1 US). [https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/new-gs1-digital-link-standard-to-help-brands-connect-consumers-with-useful-product-information-online-300696218.html]
source_note: GS1 confirms Digital Link represents GS1 keys in web URIs (Release 1.6.0, Mar 2025).

name: The Handle System
public_harm_addressed: link rot / non-persistent identifiers
adoption_penetration: The Handle System is the persistent-identifier resolution infrastructure underpinning major deployments: the DOI system (the largest Handle namespace, with ~300 million registered DOIs, which are Handles) and EIDR (~1 million digital objects in 2017). As of March 2019, 9 Multi-Primary Administrators had signed agreements with the DONA Foundation; CNRI estimates the Global Handle Registry can scale to a minimum of ~1 billion prefixes (ICANN OCTO-002, Oct 2019). [https://www.icann.org/en/system/files/files/octo-002-14oct19-en.pdf]
source_note: DONA confirms it administers the distributed Handle System (Global Handle Registry), CNRI created it in 1993.

name: Digital Object Identifier System
public_harm_addressed: non-persistent identification of content
references_builds_on: Built on The Handle System (all DOIs are Handles per the DOI Foundation FAQ); the DOI syntax/system is standardized as ISO 26324.
adoption_penetration: Approximately 300 million DOIs have been assigned to date, with around 500 DOI resolutions per second (DOI Foundation FAQ, updated Feb 2023). [https://www.doi.org/the-identifier/resources/faqs]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — A published analysis of ~1 million web references across 3.5 million STM articles found that one in five articles suffers from 'reference rot' via ordinary web links, whereas references carried by the DOI/persistent-identifier infrastructure remain actionable even when content moves, evidencing that DOIs materially reduce link rot for the scholarly record (Klein et al., PLOS ONE, 2014, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0115253). [https://www.doi.org/the-identifier/resources/faqs]
source_note: DOI Foundation confirms DOI is built on the Handle System and standardized as ISO 26324.

name: ISO/IEC 6523 Organization identification
public_harm_addressed: ambiguous identification of legal entities
adoption_penetration: 245 International Code Designators (ICDs, codes 0002-0245) are currently registered; ISO/IEC 6523 is used as the organization-identification scheme in the Peppol e-invoicing/e-procurement network (OpenPeppol official BIS Billing 3.0 documentation). [https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/codelist/ICD/]
source_note: ISO confirms ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023 structure for identification of organizations.

name: Object Identifiers (OID)
public_harm_addressed: collisions/ambiguity in registered object identifiers
references_builds_on: Governed by the ITU-T X.660-series of Recommendations (X.660, X.662, X.666, X.667, X.668, X.669, X.672) together with corresponding ISO/IEC standards.

name: Korea Pharmaceutical Information Service serialization & drug supply-history reporting (KPIS)

[https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2022.925287/full]

name: Beef Traceability Law (Act on Individual Identification of Cattle)

source_note: MAFF page confirms the Rice Traceability Act requires actors in production/distribution/sale of rice and rice products to keep records enabling quick identification of distribution routes and to provide origin information. Effective year not stated on this page (left blank rather than inferred). [Batch year-fill: 2009 (adopted/promulgated (公布) April 24, 2009 (平成21年4月24日); phased entry into force Oct 1, 2010 and Jul 1, 2011), high confidence. https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jbrewsocjapan/105/8/105_522/_pdf/-char/ja]

name: Mandatory GS1 barcode labeling for medical devices and drugs (PMD Act)

A 2019 government/GS1 Japan survey found GTIN compliance already at 100% for specified biological products and oral/injectable primary and secondary packaging, 88.9%–99.8% for medical devices, with lower rates (83.2%) for topical-medicine tertiary packaging. [https://www.gs1jp.org/assets/img/pdf/GS1seminae_Muraoka.pdf]

name: Internal Revenue Stamps Integrated System for cigarettes (IRSIS)

effectiveness_verified: inconclusive — the World Bank's global illicit-tobacco-trade review found IRSIS enabled real-time stamp tracking, a Stamp Verifier authentication app, and successful prosecutions (e.g., the Mighty Corporation case), but found no systematic before/after data showing it reduced illicit trade or raised revenue, and noted the compliance-monitoring project itself had lapsed. [https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/502721548435006600-0090022019/render/WBGTobaccoIllicitTradePhilippines.txt]

name: Chestny ZNAK (National Digital Marking and Traceability System)

[https://ninho.inca.gov.br/jspui/bitstream/123456789/16805/1/Informativo%20da%20Conicq%20-%20n%208%20-%202015-4-5.pdf]
source_note: Confirmed via official gov.br service page: SCORPIOS run by Receita Federal via Casa da Moeda; production-counting equipment plus barcode marking/tracking of cigarette output; legal basis IN RFB 769/2007 (export controls updated by IN RFB 1155/2011).

name: Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil Principles & Criteria and Supply Chain Certification Standard
public_harm_addressed: Tropical deforestation and peatland loss from palm oil
references_builds_on: ISO 17065; ISEAL Codes of Good Practice
adoption_penetration: In 2022, Certified Sustainable Palm Oil (CSPO) production exceeded 15 million MT, representing 20% of global crude palm oil production; RSPO members accounted for 42% of the 77.6 million MT of global palm oil, and certified hectarage grew +6.6% year-on-year (RSPO ACOP 2022). [https://rspo.org/acop-2022-reports-continued-progress-in-cspo-production-and-consumption-despite-global-disruptions-cspo-production-hits-15-million-mt-milestone/]
effectiveness_verified: counterproductive - Peer-reviewed evaluation (Zachlod et al., 2025, Communications Earth & Environment) found RSPO certification associated with an unintended, counterproductive decline in oil-palm plantation efficiency in Malaysia (e.g., one estate showed a 21.97 percentage-point drop in oil-palm coverage, 2018-2023). Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-025-02150-2 [https://rspo.org/acop-2022-reports-continued-progress-in-cspo-production-and-consumption-despite-global-disruptions-cspo-production-hits-15-million-mt-milestone/]
source_note: Confirmed via rspo.org: RSPO formed 2004 (WWF, MPOA, Unilever, AAK, Migros); current P&C v4.2 (2024), Supply Chain Cert Std (2020), Independent Smallholder Std v2.2 (2024).

name: RTRS Standard for Responsible Soy Production
owner: Round Table on Responsible Soy Association (RTRS)
owner_normalised: Round Table on Responsible Soy Association
public_harm_addressed: Deforestation and native-vegetation conversion from soy expansion
references_builds_on: ISEAL Codes of Good Practice; zero-deforestation/zero-conversion cutoff
adoption_penetration: In 2023, 7.5 million tonnes of RTRS-certified soy were produced on 2.2 million hectares (certified area +10.5% vs 2022); 11,480 new producers were certified during 2023, with Brazil producing ~6.4 million tonnes (RTRS, 2023). [https://responsiblesoy.org/rtrs-certification-soybean-growth-2023?lang=en]
source_note: Confirmed via responsiblesoy.org: founded 2006 in Zurich; Production Std v4.0 (2021), Chain of Custody v3.1 (2025); zero-deforestation cutoff established 2016.

name: ProTerra Standard for Sustainability and Non-GMO Certification
sector_detail: Soy, feed and food supply chains
public_harm_addressed: GMO contamination and deforestation in feed/soy chains
adoption_penetration: As of 2025/2026 (ProTerra Network directory): 160 Full Members, 86 ProTerra Certified operators, 16 Associate Members, spanning 40+ countries (largest concentrations in Brazil, Netherlands, Germany, India, Russia). Standard is now at v5.0 (2024). [https://www.proterrafoundation.org/the-proterra-network/ ; https://www.proterrafoundation.org/partnership-benchmarks/]
effectiveness_verified: No published outcome/impact evaluation (with a reduced-harm/mixed/limited/counterproductive/inconclusive verdict) located this session; ProTerra references an internal environmental-footprint study of certified vs. non-certified soy but results were not published on the linked page. [https://www.proterrafoundation.org/the-proterra-network/ ; https://www.proterrafoundation.org/partnership-benchmarks/]
source_note: Confirmed via proterrafoundation.org: established 2006; current ProTerra Certification Standard v5.0; segregated non-GMO plus sustainability. Basel Criteria origin not confirmed on this page.

name: Bonsucro Production Standard
public_harm_addressed: Water, labour and land-use harms of sugarcane production
references_builds_on: ISEAL; ISO 17065; EU Renewable Energy Directive
adoption_penetration: Bonsucro-certified sugarcane represented approximately 6.5% of global production, with 189,964 hectares added during the reporting period (Bonsucro Outcome Report 2022, covering the 2021-22 season). [https://bonsucro.com/bonsucros-latest-outcomes-revealed/]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm - Bonsucro Outcome Report 2022 (self-reported outcome data): certified operations showed a 20% improvement in irrigated water-use efficiency (2020-2021), workers paid on average 19% above the national minimum wage, and 128,000+ farm and 68,000 mill workers benefiting. [https://bonsucro.com/bonsucros-latest-outcomes-revealed/]
source_note: Confirmed via bonsucro.com: originated 2005 as Better Sugarcane Initiative, certification launched 2011; current Production Standard v5.2.1 (released Oct 2025, mandatory Jan 2026).

name: Global Organic Textile Standard
public_harm_addressed: Greenwashing of 'organic' textiles; chemical and labour harms
references_builds_on: IFOAM organic farming standards; ISO 17065; ILO core conventions
adoption_penetration: 14,676 GOTS-certified facilities across 89 countries in 2023 (an 8% increase over 2022), certified via 25 GOTS-approved certification bodies (GOTS Annual Press Release 2024). [https://global-standard.org/images/resource-library/documents/PR/2024_AnnualPR_UK.pdf]
source_note: Confirmed via official GOTS v8.0 PDF: v8.0 released March 2026, effective 1 March 2027; owner Global Standards gGmbH (Stuttgart). First version 2006 is the standard's widely-reported origin (not independently sourced this session).

name: Organic Content Standard
sector_detail: Organic cotton and non-food organic fibres
public_harm_addressed: False organic-content claims in textiles
references_builds_on: IFOAM Family of Standards (organic input); Textile Exchange Content Claim Standard
adoption_penetration: No OCS-specific certified-site or volume figure was found from an authoritative primary source this session (Textile Exchange's 2024 Materials Market Report only gives a combined figure of 75,173 sites certified in 2023 across its whole standards portfolio — GOTS, GRS, RCS, OCS, RWS, RDS, etc. — not broken out for OCS alone). [https://textileexchange.org/app/uploads/2021/02/OCS-101-V3.0-Organic-Content-Standard.pdf]
source_note: Confirmed via textileexchange.org: owned by Textile Exchange; verifies organic content plus chain of custody using IFOAM Family of Standards; current v3.0 (2020), user manual v3.1 (2021); standard document carries © 2013.

name: IFOAM Organic Guarantee System - Participatory Guarantee Systems and IFOAM Norms/Family of Standards
public_harm_addressed: Organic fraud and exclusion of smallholders from certification
references_builds_on: IFOAM Norms; Codex Alimentarius organic guidelines
adoption_penetration: 323 PGS initiatives worldwide (62 currently under development) involving 1,417,522 producers, of which 1,328,496 were certified, per IFOAM's global PGS survey (2022 data). [https://www.ifoam.bio/our-work/how/standards-certification/PGS-statistics]
source_note: Confirmed via ifoam.bio: IFOAM founded 1972 (100+ countries); official PGS definition 2008; PGS are peer-based organic quality assurance complementary to third-party certification, within the Organic Guarantee System / Family of Standards.

name: SAI Platform Farm Sustainability Assessment / Regenerating Together
public_harm_addressed: Unsustainable farming and duplicative audit burden on farmers
references_builds_on: Benchmarking/equivalence with GLOBALG.A.P. and other farm-level schemes
adoption_penetration: The FSA has enabled over 360,000 farms in 60 countries to assess and verify sustainable production across 190 cultivated crops (cumulative since 2014; current version FSA 3.0), and is benchmarked by more than 100 global sustainability schemes (SAI Platform). [https://saiplatform.org/press-area/fsa/]
source_note: Confirmed via saiplatform.org: FSA first version 2014, FSA 3.0 April 2021; Regenerating Together framework announced (press release Feb 2024), integrated standalone tool powered by FSA operations launching 2025.

name: Better Cotton Standard System
public_harm_addressed: Pesticide/water harm and labour abuse in cotton farming
references_builds_on: ISEAL Codes of Good Practice; ILO core conventions
adoption_penetration: In the 2022-23 season Better Cotton accounted for 22% of global cotton production, grown by 2.2 million licensed farmers (5.4 million tonnes, +15% year-on-year); the programme reached more than 2.8 million cotton farmers across 22 countries (Better Cotton 2022-23 Annual Report). [https://bettercotton.org/better-cotton-2022-23-annual-report-better-cotton-accounts-for-22-of-global-production/]
effectiveness_verified: limited - Independent Wageningen University endline evaluation (Pamuk, Motovska & van Rijn, 2022) of Better Cotton's impact on cotton farmers in India found the contribution of capacity-building activities to increased farmer profitability was limited (partly attributed to COVID-19 disruption of training). Source: https://research.wur.nl/en/publications/towards-sustainable-cotton-farming-validating-the-impact-of-bette/ [https://bettercotton.org/better-cotton-2022-23-annual-report-better-cotton-accounts-for-22-of-global-production/]
source_note: Confirmed via bettercotton.org: origin dated to a 2005 WWF-convened roundtable; ~2.13M licensed farmers across 22 countries; multi-stakeholder Better Cotton Standard System.

name: Non-GMO Project Standard (Non-GMO Project Verified)
public_harm_addressed: Undisclosed GMO content and consumer deception
references_builds_on: The Standard requires GMO risk testing to be performed by laboratories accredited to ISO 17025; it does not formally incorporate Codex Alimentarius, EU GMO thresholds, or organic standards into its core requirements.
adoption_penetration: As of 2025 (Non-GMO Project's own verification FAQ): the Butterfly seal covers 66,000+ unique-formula verified products representing about $48.9 billion in annual U.S. sales; 87% of surveyed ingredient suppliers with verified goods call verification an essential revenue-building strategy. [https://www.nongmoproject.org/verification-faq/]
effectiveness_verified: Not found (no third-party outcome/impact evaluation located this session). [https://www.nongmoproject.org/verification-faq/]
source_note: Confirmed via nongmoproject.org: 501(c)(3) founded 2007 by two grocers (Berkeley CA + Toronto); Butterfly 'Non-GMO Project Verified' label since 2010; North America's leading GMO-avoidance verification.

name: USDA Process Verified Program
sector_detail: Livestock, poultry, dairy, seeds & grains, produce
public_harm_addressed: Unverifiable marketing claims and consumer deception
adoption_penetration: USDA/AMS maintains a public directory of approved PVP companies (processverified.usda.gov / AMS PVP Directory), organized by commodity (beef, poultry, pork, dairy, etc.) and spanning multiple result pages; no precise total headcount is published in a single verified figure, so no adoption number is reported here. [https://www.usda.gov/about-usda/news/blog/usda-process-verified-program-transparency-farm-market-0 ; https://www.ams.usda.gov/services/auditing/pvp-directory]
source_note: Confirmed via ams.usda.gov: USDA AMS voluntary audit-based verification of documented process/marketing claims evaluated against the ISO 9000 series; covers livestock/poultry, dairy, seeds & grains, produce. Founding year not stated on the page. [Batch year-fill: 1996 (AMS Livestock and Seed (LS) Program began offering the verification service that became the USDA Process Verified Program), medium confidence. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2002/12/30/02-32806/united-states-standards-for-livestock-and-meat-marketing-claims]

name: Fair Trade Certified (Fair Trade USA standards)
sector_detail: Coffee, cocoa, produce, seafood, apparel, home goods
public_harm_addressed: Exploitative labour and unfair producer prices
adoption_penetration: Per Fair Trade USA's own impact page (2025/2026): 1.6 million Fair Trade Certified producers across 50+ countries, 1,500+ business partners, 12,500+ products bearing the label, and more than $1 billion cumulative Community Development Fund benefit distributed to farmers/workers/fishers. [https://www.fairtradecertified.org/what-we-do/our-impact/ ; https://warrington.ufl.edu/news/fair-trade-paradox/ ; https://www.fairtradecertified.org/news/fair-trade-accepted-as-iseal-member/]
effectiveness_verified: Mixed. A University of Florida study (Daehoon Jung, forthcoming in Production and Operations Management; published Sept. 9, 2025) explicitly analyzing competition between Fair Trade USA and Fairtrade America found that competition expands consumer access to fair-trade products but simultaneously erodes the per-unit premium individual farmers receive ('mainstreaming'/'fairwashing' trade-off) — more farmers participate, but each captures a smaller benefit. [https://www.fairtradecertified.org/what-we-do/our-impact/ ; https://warrington.ufl.edu/news/fair-trade-paradox/ ; https://www.fairtradecertified.org/news/fair-trade-accepted-as-iseal-member/]
source_note: Confirmed via fairtradecertified.org: founded 1998 as TransFair USA; separated from Fairtrade International in 2012; Fair Trade Certified spans food, apparel, home goods and seafood.

name: Friend of the Sea Sustainable Seafood Certification
owner: World Sustainability Organization (Friend of the Sea)
public_harm_addressed: Overfishing and unsustainable aquaculture
references_builds_on: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries; ISO 17065 accreditation
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
source_note: Confirmed via friendofthesea.org: created 2008 by Paolo Bray, now a project of the World Sustainability Organization; certifies fisheries, aquaculture, fishmeal & Omega-3; ISO 17065-accredited third-party audits.

name: GCP Coffee Sustainability Reference Code (formerly Baseline Common Code)
public_harm_addressed: Fragmentation of coffee sustainability claims; child/forced labour and deforestation
references_builds_on: Common Code for the Coffee Community (2004); ISEAL; ILO conventions
adoption_penetration: As of December 2024 (Global Coffee Platform announcement): 27 coffee sustainability schemes/standards have been formally recognized as equivalent/aligned with the Reference Code (4 under third-party assurance, 23 under second-party assurance). [https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/latest/2024/four-more-coffee-sustainability-schemes-aligning-on-common-sustainability-language/ ; https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/our-work/coffee-sustainability-reference-code/]
effectiveness_verified: Not found (no outcome/impact evaluation of the Reference Code itself located this session). [https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/latest/2024/four-more-coffee-sustainability-schemes-aligning-on-common-sustainability-language/ ; https://www.globalcoffeeplatform.org/our-work/coffee-sustainability-reference-code/]
source_note: Confirmed via globalcoffeeplatform.org: GCP evolved from the 4C Association in 2016; Baseline Common Code v3.0 renamed the Coffee Sustainability Reference Code in 2021; functions as a sector-wide baseline for benchmarking other schemes.

name: 4C Certification (Common Code for the Coffee Community)
public_harm_addressed: Child/forced labour and deforestation in coffee production
references_builds_on: GCP Coffee Sustainability Reference Code; ILO conventions
adoption_penetration: As of December 31, 2024 (4C Services 'In Numbers'): 196 producer groups 4C certified, ~300,000 coffee producers (94% smallholders) across 19 countries, covering roughly 800,000–880,000 hectares, producing 29.1–30.5 million 60kg bags of certified green coffee. [https://www.4c-services.org/4c-impact/4c-in-numbers-2/]
effectiveness_verified: Not found (no independent outcome evaluation specific to current 4C certification located this session, though 4C notes continued market demand growth in 2024). [https://www.4c-services.org/4c-impact/4c-in-numbers-2/]
source_note: Confirmed via 4c-services.org: Common Code launched 2004; became an independent third-party scheme under 4C Services (from CAS in 2018, fully independent 2020); Code of Conduct v5.0 (2025), recognized as equivalent to the GCP Coffee SR Code.

name: Bettercoal Code and Assurance System
public_harm_addressed: Unsafe, polluting and exploitative coal mining
references_builds_on: OECD Guidelines for MNEs, UN Guiding Principles, ILO conventions
adoption_penetration: Per Bettercoal's own current producer listing: 6 Bettercoal Producers across 4 countries (Colombia, Germany, USA, South Africa), each having completed site assessment and an agreed Continuous Improvement Plan against the Bettercoal Code. [https://www.bettercoal.org/bettercoal-producers]
source_note: Confirmed on Bettercoal site: 12-principle/144-provision ESG Code, on-site assessment every 4 years, run by RECOSI not-for-profit; 2012 founding confirmed via Fortum Apr-2012 membership release.

name: Cobalt Industry Responsible Assessment Framework
public_harm_addressed: Child labour and human-rights harms in cobalt (esp. DRC ASM)
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: No precise verified count of participating companies was found this session; the Cobalt Institute states only that 'a significant number' of its members committed to adopting CIRAF. [https://www.cobaltinstitute.org/news/ciraf-update-reporting-obligation-hiatus/ ; https://responsiblecobalt.org/ciraf/]
effectiveness_verified: Limited. In 2025 the Cobalt Institute itself announced a hiatus on CIRAF participants' annual public reporting obligation while it reviews the framework's future in light of new mandatory due-diligence regulation — i.e., the scheme's own transparency mechanism was suspended by its administrator. [https://www.cobaltinstitute.org/news/ciraf-update-reporting-obligation-hiatus/ ; https://responsiblecobalt.org/ciraf/]
source_note: Cobalt Institute confirms development from 2017, pilot 2018; OECD-aligned self-assessment with independent verification and public disclosure. Note: Cobalt Institute later placed CIRAF reporting obligation on hiatus.

name: Responsible Cobalt Initiative
owner: CCCMC (China Chamber of Commerce of Metals, Minerals & Chemicals); co-founded with OECD; standard now co-managed with Responsible Minerals Initiative (RMI)
owner_normalised: CCCMC ; co-founded with OECD; standard now co-managed with Responsible Minerals Initiative
public_harm_addressed: Child labour and human-rights harms in cobalt supply chains
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance, Chinese Due Diligence Guidelines (CCCMC)
adoption_penetration: No verified member-company count located this session. [https://respect.international/responsible-cobalt-initiative-rci/ ; https://www.responsiblebusiness.org/news/rmi-rci/]
source_note: Confirmed RCI established 2016 by CCCMC and OECD to improve cobalt supply-chain governance; aligns members to OECD and CCCMC guidelines. RMI+RCI jointly publish the Cobalt Refiner Supply Chain Due Diligence Standard.

name: ICGLR Regional Certification Mechanism
owner: International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR)
owner_normalised: International Conference on the Great Lakes Region
public_harm_addressed: Conflict minerals financing armed groups and rights abuses
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Minerals
adoption_penetration: No current verified figures on number of certified mines or certificate volumes were found this session; the RCM's own 2nd-edition manual (2024) is a procedural document without implementation statistics, and the only located historical figures (DRC/Rwanda's first certificates, 2012–2013) are over a decade old. [https://icglr.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/ICGLR-Regional-Certification-Mechanism-Manual-2nd-Edition_Final.pdf]
source_note: 2nd-Edition RCM Manual (approved Oct 2019) confirms: framework first developed 2011, covers 3TG across 12 ICGLR member states, explicitly incorporates OECD Due Diligence Guidance.

name: LME Policy on Responsible Sourcing of LME-Listed Brands
public_harm_addressed: Irresponsibly sourced metals traded on global markets
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance; recognises RMAP, LBMA, RJC, Copper Mark
adoption_penetration: Per the LME's own 2024 compliance update: the policy covers 435 LME-listed brands across nine physically settled contracts in 54 countries. As of the December 31, 2023 compliance deadline, approximately 90% of brands had submitted the required compliance information. [https://www.lme.com/-/media/Files/About/Responsibility/Responsible-sourcing/BRANDS-GENERAL-24-005-2024-UPDATE-ON-RESPONSIBLE-SOURCING-REPORTING-FOR-LME-LISTED-BRANDS.pdf?sc_lang=en]
effectiveness_verified: Mixed. The same LME reporting shows roughly 10% of listed brands were non-compliant and scheduled for suspension/delisting for failing to meet the policy's requirements — i.e., partial but incomplete compliance uptake industry-wide. [https://www.lme.com/-/media/Files/About/Responsibility/Responsible-sourcing/BRANDS-GENERAL-24-005-2024-UPDATE-ON-RESPONSIBLE-SOURCING-REPORTING-FOR-LME-LISTED-BRANDS.pdf?sc_lang=en]
source_note: LME confirms responsible-sourcing rules in Part 7 of Rulebook, introduced Oct 2019, mandatory for all LME-listed brands (red-flag assessment, OECD alignment), phased to full compliance by 2022-2023.

name: Chinese Due Diligence Guidelines for Responsible Mineral Supply Chains
owner: China Chamber of Commerce of Metals, Minerals & Chemicals Importers & Exporters (CCCMC)
owner_normalised: China Chamber of Commerce of Metals
public_harm_addressed: Conflict, human-rights and misconduct harms in mineral supply chains
references_builds_on: OECD Due Diligence Guidance, UN Guiding Principles on Business & Human Rights
adoption_penetration: No verified quantitative adoption figure (number of implementing companies) was found this session. [https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/blog/responsible-mineral-supply-chain-efforts-in-china-progress-and-challenges/]
effectiveness_verified: Limited. Business & Human Rights Resource Centre's China mineral-supply-chain analysis states that 'not enough Chinese companies are aware of the CCCMC guidelines' and that due-diligence uptake remains far from mainstream in China, citing weak incentives around the voluntary standard. [https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/blog/responsible-mineral-supply-chain-efforts-in-china-progress-and-challenges/]
source_note: Confirmed CCCMC-issued guidelines (first edition 2015; 2nd edition 2023-24) explicitly built on OECD Guidance and UNGPs; extend CCCMC social-responsibility guidelines for outbound mining. China-origin with global supply-chain reach.

name: Sustainable Forestry Initiative Forest Management Standard
public_harm_addressed: Unsustainable logging, biodiversity and water-quality loss
adoption_penetration: FIDO Alliance's 2024 consumer survey: 53% of people report having enabled passkeys on at least one of their accounts, and 22% enable them on every account they can. FIDO cites production deployment outcomes including Google's ~4x improvement in sign-in success rate vs. passwords and CVS Health's 98% reduction in mobile account-takeover fraud.
compliance_cost: FIDO2 / WebAuthn specifications are open and royalty-free.
source_note: SFI site confirms current 2022 Forest Management Standard (13 principles/17 objectives/141 indicators), operates in US & Canada, third-party audited; PEFC page confirms SFI is a PEFC national member and PEFC-endorsed (mutual recognition).

name: Sustainable Biomass Program
public_harm_addressed: Unsustainable forest harvesting and mis-stated carbon for energy biomass
references_builds_on: ISO 17065/17011/19011; EU Renewable Energy Directive; recognises FSC/PEFC feedstock
adoption_penetration: Per SBP's own Annual Review 2024: 340 certificate holders at year-end 2024 (+25% year-on-year), 19.15 million tonnes of SBP-certified biomass produced and sold in 2024 (+28% YoY; 17.65 million tonnes consumed in Europe, +30% YoY), operations spanning 35 countries, with the scheme transitioning to SBP Standards v2.0. [https://sbp-cert.org/sbp-publishes-annual-review-2024/ ; https://news.mongabay.com/2025/08/sustainable-biomass-certification-scheme-is-flawed-degrades-forests-report-finds/]
effectiveness_verified: Counterproductive. A July 2025 report by forest-governance expert Richard Robertson (commissioned by Solutions for Our Climate, Global Environmental Forum, Mighty Earth, Biofuelwatch, and the Environmental Paper Network) found SBP certifies pellet mills and biomass traders largely through desk-based review rather than field audits or direct engagement with logging companies; that over 90% of certified biomass is not rigorously verified at source; that it accepts feedstock from ecologically important primary forests; and that its carbon accounting treats biomass emissions as zero — concluding the scheme provides 'a veneer of legitimacy' that enables continued forest degradation. [https://sbp-cert.org/sbp-publishes-annual-review-2024/ ; https://news.mongabay.com/2025/08/sustainable-biomass-certification-scheme-is-flawed-degrades-forests-report-finds/]
source_note: SBP site confirms independent certification of legal/sustainable woody feedstock with chain-of-custody via Data Transfer System, references ISO 17065/19011/17011; timeline page confirms SBP created 2013 to continue Initiative of Wood Pellet Buyers (IWPB).

name: CITES Timber Species Listings (Appendices I/II/III)
owner: CITES Secretariat / Conference of the Parties (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, UNEP-administered)
owner_normalised: CITES Secretariat / Conference of the Parties
public_harm_addressed: Overexploitation and extinction risk for endangered tree species
adoption_penetration: CITES regulates international trade in close to 800 tree species across Appendices I, II and III (current figure per CITES Secretariat). New Appendix II listings covering additional timber genera (e.g., Cordia, Handroanthus, Dipteryx) took effect November 25, 2024. [https://cites.org/eng/topics/flora/cites-and-forests]
effectiveness_verified: Not found from an authoritative primary source this session. [https://cites.org/eng/topics/flora/cites-and-forests]
source_note: US FWS confirms CITES timber listings require export permits and proof of legal sourcing; recent Appendix-II additions (effective 25 Nov 2024) include Handroanthus/ipe, Dipteryx/cumaru, Afzelia, Pterocarpus/padauk, Paubrasilia. Convention in force since 1975; major timber listings expanded at CoP17 (2016)-CoP19 (2022).

name: IPC-1782 Standard for Manufacturing and Supply Chain Traceability of Electronic Products
public_harm_addressed: Counterfeit and unsafe electronic components; poor recall/defect tracing
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
source_note: Confirmed IPC-published single traceability standard (first 2016; Rev A 2020; Rev B Sept 2023), risk-based levels tied to IPC classes, covers internal and external traceability and counterfeit reduction.

name: EPEAT Ecolabel and Registry
owner: Global Electronics Council (GEC, formerly Green Electronics Council)
public_harm_addressed: E-waste, hazardous materials and unsustainable electronics
adoption_penetration: Almost 300 million EPEAT-registered products are purchased annually worldwide; about 2.7 billion have been sold cumulatively since the registry launched in 2006; EPEAT is used as a procurement criterion in 50+ countries. [https://www.epeat.net/]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — EPEAT's own cumulative impact accounting (2006-2023, via its Benefits Calculator) attributes $34 billion in purchaser cost savings and 341 million tonnes of GHG emissions avoided to EPEAT-registered product purchases. [https://www.epeat.net/]
source_note: GEC site confirms EPEAT registry/ecolabel with Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers and third-party verification across full lifecycle. Britannica confirms EPEAT created 2003, launched 2006, GEC-overseen, ANSI/IEEE-rooted criteria, required in US federal procurement (2007 Executive Order).

name: Responsible Business Alliance Code of Conduct
owner: Responsible Business Alliance (RBA; formerly Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition, EICC)
public_harm_addressed: Forced/child labour and unsafe conditions in electronics manufacturing
references_builds_on: ILO Fundamental Conventions, UN Guiding Principles, OECD Guidelines, UDHR
adoption_penetration: 600+ member companies with combined annual revenues over $8 trillion, employing 21.5+ million people, with products manufactured across 120+ countries (RBA, current). [https://www.responsiblebusiness.org/code-of-conduct/]
effectiveness_verified: Not found from an authoritative primary source this session. [https://www.responsiblebusiness.org/code-of-conduct/]
source_note: RBA Code v8.0 confirms five sections (Labor, Health & Safety, Environmental, Ethics, Management Systems) aligned to ILO/UNGP/OECD; verified via shared audit (VAP/RBA-Online). RBA rebrand page confirms EICC founded 2004, renamed RBA 2017.

name: Higg Index (Cascale)
owner: Cascale (formerly Sustainable Apparel Coalition); delivered via Worldly platform
public_harm_addressed: Unmeasured environmental and social impacts / greenwashing in apparel
references_builds_on: Life-cycle assessment data; SAC/Cascale facility, brand and product tools
adoption_penetration: About 40,000 active Higg Index users; Cascale's ~300 member organizations (brands, retailers, manufacturers) represent roughly half of the global apparel and footwear industry (Cascale, current). [https://www.businessoffashion.com/articles/sustainability/higg-index-fashion-greenwashing-regulation-sustainability-sustainable-apparel-coalition/]
effectiveness_verified: mixed — Norway's Consumer Authority ruled in 2022 that Higg-based sustainability product profiles (used by the Sustainable Apparel Coalition/Cascale and H&M Group) were 'misleading,' finding the underlying data 'oversimplified, inaccurate and imprecise'; this prompted suspension of the consumer-facing Higg-based label and ongoing methodology overhaul. [https://www.businessoffashion.com/articles/sustainability/higg-index-fashion-greenwashing-regulation-sustainability-sustainable-apparel-coalition/]
source_note: Cascale confirms SAC founded 2009 by Walmart & Patagonia, Higg Index suite launched 2011, SAC rebranded to Cascale on 26 Feb 2024; Higg tools spun into Worldly (2019) as exclusive platform; measures social/environmental performance across value chain.

name: Responsible Down Standard
public_harm_addressed: Animal cruelty (live-plucking, force-feeding) in down supply chains
references_builds_on: Textile Exchange Content Claim Standard; Five Freedoms of animal welfare
adoption_penetration: 97% of card-present transactions globally were conducted using EMV chip technology, as most recently reported for Q4 2025 by EMVCo — figures compiled from its six member networks (American Express, Discover, JCB, Mastercard, UnionPay, Visa). Contactless is tracked on the same deployment page but published only in downloadable image files, not as extractable text.
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm: Randomized rollout across 157 subdistricts / ~19 million people (Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar, 'Building State Capacity,' AER 2016): biometric smartcards produced a faster, more predictable, less corrupt NREGS payment process with a significant reduction in leakage of funds AND no reduction in beneficiary access; beneficiary time savings alone equalled the intervention's cost, and beneficiaries strongly preferred the system. Direction: reduced leakage without causing exclusion — the positive counter-case showing outcomes hinge on implementation/design, not the technology alone.
compliance_cost: Chip and terminal upgrade costs are borne by issuers, acquirers and merchants; global rollout was driven by the card networks' fraud liability-shift rules rather than a certification fee.
source_note: Textile Exchange confirms RDS launched 2014 (co-developed by The North Face), third-party certified with transparent/traceable chain of custody, bans live-plucking and force-feeding, requires Five Freedoms; RDS 3.0 first substantial revision.

effectiveness_verified: Not found from an authoritative primary source this session. [https://textileexchange.org/knowledge-center/reports/materials-market-report-2024/]
source_note: Textile Exchange confirms RWS is a voluntary standard certifying all sites from farm to final B2B seller across animal welfare (Five Freedoms), land management and social welfare with chain of custody; first released 2016 (RWS 2.0 March 2020).

name: PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System
public_harm_addressed: double-counting or misrepresented generation attributes (fuel source, emissions)

adoption_penetration: As of July 31, 2024: 436,583 registered generators, 28,100 account holders, and 95,316,892 certificates issued since the system's 2005 launch. PJM-GATS is one of three U.S. "all-generation" tracking systems and ranks third by certificate volume behind M-RETS (355.7M) and NAR (264.5M). In Feb. 2023 PJM-EIS announced it would begin issuing hourly, timestamped certificates. PJM-GATS) "have succeeded" in preventing double-counting of renewable energy certificates and "help bolster market credibility" and REC liquidity, via single-registration rules, whole-EAC requirements, cross-system retirement on import/export, and automated production-ceiling checks. The same report flags gaps — sparse hourly data, thin non-renewable emissions tracking, low geographic granularity — as areas for future evolution rather than as current failures. [https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-01/status_and_trends_report_us_energy_attribute_tracking_systems.pdf]

references_builds_on: SALEEM (Saudi Product Safety Program), GCC technical regulations
adoption_penetration: As of February 2019 (SASO's own announcement), more than 5,000 commercial facilities/local factories had enrolled and over 60,000 consumer products had been registered on the Saber platform, initially covering gas appliances/accessories with further product categories phased in afterward. [https://www.saso.gov.sa/en/mediacenter/news/Pages/saso_news_967.aspx]
effectiveness_verified: Not verified this session (no more recent official statistics located). [https://www.saso.gov.sa/en/mediacenter/news/Pages/saso_news_967.aspx]
source_note: saber.sa confirms a government electronic platform operated under SASO for product registration and issuance of product/shipment conformity certificates for importers, local manufacturers and government entities, with a supplier-name-on-product requirement from 1 October 2026. [Batch year-fill: 2019 (launched / entered into force), high confidence. https://www.saso.gov.sa/en/mediacenter/news/Pages/saso_news_953.aspx]

name: Global LEI System — Legal Entity Identifier & verifiable LEI
public_harm_addressed: opaque counterparties, systemic risk, fraud, inability to identify who you deal with
references_builds_on: ISO 17442, FSB/G20 mandate, vLEI on W3C VC / ACDC
adoption_penetration: Global LEI population passed 1 million (2017), 2 million (2022), and 2.6 million active LEIs by 2024 (+84% vs. 2019, per FSB); GLEIF reports 2.93 million+ active LEIs in 2025 with 13.5% annual growth (up from 11.5% in 2024) and 355,000+ new LEIs issued that year. [https://www.fsb.org/2024/10/implementation-of-the-legal-entity-identifier-progress-report/]
effectiveness_verified: mixed — FSB's October 2024 progress report finds the LEI well-established in derivatives and securities markets, but states 'broader adoption of the LEI in cross-border payments remains challenging,' citing cost barriers (especially in low-income jurisdictions) and weak incentives; it notes 'some jurisdictions have made no tangible progress' and reiterates its 2022 recommendations for fuller implementation. [https://www.fsb.org/2024/10/implementation-of-the-legal-entity-identifier-progress-report/]
source_note: gleif.org confirms GLEIF is a supra-national non-profit created in 2014 by the Financial Stability Board, overseen by the ROC (regulators from 50+ countries), operating the Global LEI Index; the vLEI is described as the verifiable/digital counterpart to the LEI.

name: Modular Open Source Identity Platform
public_harm_addressed: lack of legal identity and exclusion; vendor lock-in in national ID systems
references_builds_on: open identity standards (OpenID, W3C, ISO ID building blocks)
adoption_penetration: MOSIP's own site reports 29 country engagements and 13 national rollouts (2025–26). Independent trade coverage (Biometric Update, citing MOSIP data) reported MOSIP-based systems had issued over 100 million digital/civil identities across 11 countries in Africa and Asia by December 2023, up from 71.1 million across 6 countries in September 2022. [https://www.mosip.io/]
source_note: mosip.io confirms a modular open-source foundational digital identity platform established in 2018 at IIIT Bangalore, with 29 country engagements, 13 national rollouts and 125+ commercial technology partners.

name: Metre Convention (Convention du Mètre)
public_harm_addressed: incomparable, non-equivalent measurements across borders
adoption_penetration: Signed in 1875; as of the current BIPM listing there are 67 Member States and 36 Associate States and Economies party to the treaty. [https://www.bipm.org/en/member-states]
effectiveness_verified: Not applicable (foundational treaty, not a program with harm-reduction outcomes). [https://www.bipm.org/en/member-states]
source_note: BIPM page confirms signed 20 May 1875 by 17 states (amended 1921); created the BIPM and the CGPM/CIPM governance bodies for world measurement.

name: International System of Units (SI Brochure, 9th edition)
owner: BIPM / CGPM (Bureau International des Poids et Mesures)
public_harm_addressed: unreliable/non-traceable quantities in trade, health, safety
adoption_penetration: 9th edition published by BIPM in 2019, implementing the 2018 CGPM resolution that redefined the SI base units; used globally through BIPM's network of National Metrology Institutes and Regional Metrology Organizations (AFRIMETS, APMP, COOMET, EURAMET, GULFMET, SIM). [https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure]
source_note: BIPM confirms SI Brochure 9th ed. (2019) defines the seven base units via fixed constants; revised SI took effect 20 May 2019 (26th CGPM).

name: OIML Certification System
owner: OIML / BIML (International Organization of Legal Metrology)
public_harm_addressed: duplicated instrument type testing, unreliable instruments reaching market
references_builds_on: OIML B 18:2016; OIML Recommendations; ISO/IEC 17025; ISO/IEC 17065
adoption_penetration: Per the OIML-CS report in OIML Bulletin 2026-01: 292 OIML certificates issued in 2024 (up from 249 in 2020); 14 OIML Issuing Authorities and 38 Utilizers/Associates participating as of 2025.
compliance_cost: Manufacturers pay certification/testing fees to an OIML Issuing Authority; a single OIML certificate is designed to be reused for type approval across participating economies, reducing duplicative national testing.
source_note: OIML confirms OIML-CS launched 1 Jan 2018 under OIML B 18:2016, replacing the OIML Basic Certificate System and MAA; issues/registers OIML type-evaluation certificates via Scheme A (accredited/peer-assessed) and Scheme B.

name: OIML R 76 Non-automatic weighing instruments
public_harm_addressed: short-measure fraud and inaccurate weighing in commerce
adoption_penetration: As of September 2023, only 13 of OIML's 63 member countries (India newly admitted as the 13th, alongside Australia, Switzerland, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, France, UK, Japan, Netherlands, Sweden, Slovakia) hold Issuing Authority status able to issue internationally recognized OIML-CS certificates covering R76, alongside R35, R49 and R117. [https://wema.co.in/weighing-industry-in-market-expansion-mode/]
source_note: Fetched OIML R 76 (1993 ed., Amd.1 1995) Part 2 PDF; sets metrological/technical requirements and pattern-evaluation report format for type approval of non-automatic weighing instruments (later revised as R 76-1:2006).

name: OIML R 117 Dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water
sector_detail: legal metrology / fuel and liquid dispensing trade
public_harm_addressed: short-measure fraud at fuel pumps and liquid metering systems
adoption_penetration: Current edition OIML R 117:2019 published by OIML TC 8/SC 3 Project Group 4, approved by the International Committee of Legal Metrology at its 54th meeting. As of Sept 2023, R117 certification (like R76/R49/R35) could be issued by only 13 of OIML's 63 member-country Issuing Authorities. [https://www.oiml.org/en/files/pdf_r/r117-e19.pdf]
source_note: Fetched OIML R 117 (Edition 2019) PDF; establishes metrological/technical requirements for dynamic measuring systems for non-water liquids (e.g. fuel dispensers, petroleum metering).

name: OIML R 49 Water meters for cold potable water and hot water
public_harm_addressed: inaccurate water metering and unfair consumer billing
adoption_penetration: Latest edition OIML R 49:2024 published; as of Sept 2023, R49 certification (like R76/R117/R35) could be issued by only 13 of OIML's 63 member-country Issuing Authorities. [https://www.oiml.org/en/files/pdf_r/r049-1-e13.pdf]
source_note: Fetched OIML R 49-1 (Edition 2024) PDF Part 1; sets metrological/technical requirements for water meters for cold potable and hot water.

name: ISO 17034 General requirements for the competence of reference material producers
public_harm_addressed: unreliable certified reference values biasing measurements and test results
adoption_penetration: Became publicly available November 1, 2016. The Asia Pacific Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (APLAC) mandated a 3-year transition, requiring all accredited Reference Material Producers among its accreditation-body signatories (e.g., A2LA) to transition to the new standard by November 1, 2019. [https://a2la.org/transition-period-for-iso-17034-2016-implementation-established-for-accredited-reference-materials-producers/]
source_note: ISO catalogue (accessed via search) confirms ISO 17034:2016, 1st edition, 'General requirements for the competence of reference material producers'; the accreditation basis for CRM/RMP competence.

name: WELMEC European Cooperation in Legal Metrology
owner: WELMEC e.V. (European Cooperation in Legal Metrology)
public_harm_addressed: divergent national instrument approval and consumer measurement fraud in the single market
references_builds_on: EU Measuring Instruments Directive 2014/32/EU; OIML Recommendations
adoption_penetration: Created June 1990 via a Memorandum of Understanding originally signed by 18 countries; grown to more than 30 member organisations across EU/EFTA states; formalized as a legal entity, WELMEC e.V. (Braunschweig, Germany), since September 2020. [https://www.welmec.org/about-welmec/about-us]
source_note: WELMEC site confirms founded 1990 (MoU, 18 countries; now 30+ members), incorporated as WELMEC e.V. under German law (2019/2020); produces guides recognised by the European Commission giving presumption of conformity under the MID.

name: EURAMET European Association of National Metrology Institutes
public_harm_addressed: measurements not traceable to SI or comparable across Europe
adoption_penetration: 38 member national metrology institutes, per the Czech Metrology Institute's EURAMET membership page (accessed 2026); EURAMET covers NMIs of nearly all EU/EFTA and wider European states. [https://cmi.gov.cz/node/559?language=en ; https://www.euramet.org/about-euramet]
source_note: EURAMET confirms founded 11 Jan 2007 (26 signatories, successor to EUROMET) as the Regional Metrology Organisation for Europe; peer-reviews CMCs and coordinates comparisons under the CIPM MRA.

name: Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (JCGM 100)
owner: JCGM (Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology)
public_harm_addressed: unstated/inconsistent measurement uncertainty leading to wrong conformity decisions
adoption_penetration: Jointly published/endorsed by 8 international bodies (BIPM, IEC, IFCC, ILAC, ISO, IUPAC, IUPAP, OIML); first issued 1993/95, reissued unchanged as JCGM 100:2008 — the baseline uncertainty standard referenced by accreditation frameworks (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025) worldwide. [https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf]
source_note: BIPM/JCGM publications page confirms JCGM 100:2008 GUM plus supplements (JCGM 101/102/106, GUM-1:2023, GUM-6:2020); published by the JCGM (BIPM, OIML, ISO, IEC, IUPAC, IUPAP, IFCC, ILAC).

name: International Vocabulary of Metrology (JCGM 200 / VIM)
owner: JCGM (Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology)
public_harm_addressed: ambiguous metrology terms causing miscommunicated/misused measurement results
adoption_penetration: Co-published by the same 8 organizations (BIPM, IEC, IFCC, ILAC, ISO, IUPAC, IUPAP, OIML) as the standard reference vocabulary for metrology; 3rd edition issued 2012. [https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_200_2012.pdf]
source_note: BIPM/JCGM publications page confirms JCGM 200:2012 (VIM, 3rd ed.), 'International Vocabulary of Metrology - Basic and general concepts and associated terms', published by the JCGM.

name: NIST Handbook 44 - Specifications, Tolerances and Technical Requirements for Weighing and Measuring Devices
owner: NIST / NCWM (US National Institute of Standards and Technology; National Conference on Weights and Measures)
sector_detail: legal metrology / US commercial weights and measures
public_harm_addressed: inaccurate commercial weighing/measuring devices overcharging consumers
adoption_penetration: Adopted by all 50 US states (each adopting the current or an earlier edition) as the legal basis for weights-and-measures regulation; a new edition is published annually, current is NIST HB44-2026. [https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/nist-handbooks-and-ncwm-brief-history]
source_note: NIST confirms HB 44 (2026 ed., published 5 Jan 2026; annual since 1949), developed by NCWM Committee on Specifications and Tolerances with NIST, adopted into law by US state/local weights-and-measures jurisdictions.

name: Aadhaar (Unique Identity Number) / UIDAI
owner: Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Ministry of Electronics & IT
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud, ghost/duplicate beneficiaries, welfare exclusion
references_builds_on: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act 2016
adoption_penetration: 1,448,910,429 Aadhaar numbers generated (cumulative) and 1,624,427,050 Aadhaar updates, per the live UIDAI Aadhaar Dashboard (accessed July 2026) — effectively universal coverage of India's ~1.4 billion residents.
compliance_cost: Enrollment is free to residents; program costs are borne by UIDAI/the Government of India.
source_note: UIDAI site confirms it is a statutory authority under the Aadhaar Act 2016 (est. 12 Jul 2016), issuing a 12-digit number (first Aadhaar 2010; 142cr+ generated) with authentication and e-KYC services.

name: eSign Online Electronic Signature Service
owner: Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA), Ministry of Electronics & IT
public_harm_addressed: document forgery, signature repudiation, transaction fraud
references_builds_on: IT Act 2000; RCAI PKI; Aadhaar e-KYC
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
source_note: CCA site confirms eSign is an API-integrated online digital-signature service using e-KYC under the IT Act 2000; CCA gazette page shows first eSign rules (GSR 61(E)) notified 27 Jan 2015.

name: DigiLocker
owner: National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics & IT
public_harm_addressed: fake certificates/documents, forgery, verification friction
references_builds_on: IT Act 2000; Digital Locker Rules 2016; Aadhaar
adoption_penetration: 70+ crore (700M+) registered users and 900+ crore (9B+) documents issued by 900+ issuer organizations, per the official DigiLocker site (July 2026); India Stack separately cites 4.6 billion+ documents issued directly by 1,460 registered issuer institutions. [https://www.digilocker.gov.in/ ; https://indiastack.org/identity.html]
source_note: NeGD confirms DigiLocker launched 1 Jul 2015 under Digital India; issued documents carry the same legal weight as originals under the IT Act 2000 and Digital Locker Rules 2016.

name: Root Certifying Authority of India
owner: Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA), Ministry of Electronics & IT
public_harm_addressed: untrusted certificates, man-in-the-middle, invalid digital signatures
adoption_penetration: 23 licensed Certifying Authorities currently operate under the RCAI hierarchy, per CCA's official Licensed CA disclosure list. [https://cca.gov.in/rcai.html ; https://cca.gov.in/licensed_ca.html]
source_note: CCA site confirms RCAI is the national root established under IT Act 2000 s.18(b) that digitally signs licensed CAs' public keys; the RCAI Certification Practice Statement dates from 2002.

name: DIVOC (Digital Infrastructure for Verifiable Open Credentialing)
public_harm_addressed: fake vaccination/health certificates, cross-border verification failure
references_builds_on: W3C Verifiable Credentials; WHO Smart Vaccination Certificate standards
adoption_penetration: 2 billion vaccination certificates issued across 5 countries (India, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Jamaica, Indonesia) by Sept 2021; certificate format accepted/recognized in 96-120 countries, used by over one-fifth of world population, with system capacity of ~25 million certificates/day. [https://egov.org.in/articles/the-road-to-2-billion/]
effectiveness_verified: WHO granted DIVOC formal compliance certification against the Digital Documentation of COVID-19 Certificates (DDCC) standard (2021), and it is recognized as a Digital Public Good by the DPGA — this is an interoperability/compliance verification, not an independent harm-reduction outcome study. [https://egov.org.in/articles/the-road-to-2-billion/]
source_note: DIVOC site confirms it is an open-source digital public good by eGov Foundation; issued 2bn+ digitally-signed COVID certificates via CoWIN and deployed in Sri Lanka, Philippines, Indonesia and Jamaica.

name: National Network Identity Authentication Public Service (Cyberspace ID / 网号-网证)
owner: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and Ministry of Public Security (MPS)
owner_normalised: Cyberspace Administration of China and Ministry of Public Security
public_harm_addressed: over-collection of personal data, identity theft, data breaches
references_builds_on: Cybersecurity Law; PIPL; Measures on Management of National Network Identity Authentication Public Service
adoption_penetration: GS1 states that 'over two million companies around the world' use GS1 Standards (GTINs/barcodes) to identify products and manage supply chains; the GS1 system operates through 120+ national member organisations worldwide (accessed Jul 2026).
effectiveness_verified: mixed: Peer-reviewed audit (Parsovs, USENIX Security 2020) of Estonia's national e-ID card found systemic key-management failures: 700,000+ cards exposed to the 2017 ROCA RSA-factorization vulnerability (forcing mass certificate suspension), plus duplicate private keys shared across different cardholders and private keys generated off-chip — enabling impersonation, signature forgery, and unauthorized decryption. Direction: a centralized national digital ID delivers services at scale but concentrates catastrophic, demonstrated data-leakage/impersonation risk when key management fails.
source_note: CAC official text confirms the Measures were jointly issued by six departments (incl. MPS and CAC) and take effect 15 Jul 2025, establishing the 网号/网证 (web number/web credential) federated authentication service.

name: CTID / Cyber Trusted Identity (网络身份认证 / 网证)
owner: Ministry of Public Security First Research Institute (公安部第一研究所)
owner_normalised: Ministry of Public Security First Research Institute
public_harm_addressed: ID-card number exposure, impersonation, data leakage
references_builds_on: Resident Identity Card Law; GB national standards
adoption_penetration: 40 million (4000万) people had applied for the national network ID (网号/网证) as of July 2026, one year after the 'National Network Identity Authentication Public Service Management Measures' took effect (15 July 2025); the service has provided free authentication to 400+ government departments/regulators, local governments, enterprises and major internet platforms, per Ministry of Public Security reporting. [https://www.stdaily.com/web/gdxw/2026-07/14/content_547250.html]
effectiveness_verified: MPS/state-media reporting frames it as reduced-harm for personal-information exposure ('实名不显名' — verified without displaying the underlying name/ID number) to curb identity-data leakage; this is the issuing agency's own claim, not an independent audit. [https://www.stdaily.com/web/gdxw/2026-07/14/content_547250.html]
source_note: China Daily confirms the CTID network-ID credential (网证) is developed and run by the MPS First Research Institute, piloted 2018 via Alipay in Quzhou/Hangzhou/Fuzhou, mapping to the resident ID card without exposing personal data.

name: RealDID (Real-name Decentralized Identifier)
owner: Ministry of Public Security First Research Institute with Blockchain-based Service Network (BSN)
owner_normalised: Ministry of Public Security First Research Institute with Blockchain-based Service Network
public_harm_addressed: personal-data linkage and leakage, impersonation
adoption_penetration: No published figure identified (checked)
source_note: CoinDesk (citing BSN) confirms the MPS First Research Institute and BSN launched RealDID in Dec 2023 as the 'world's first national-level real-name decentralized identity system' enabling anonymous DID login.

name: Blockchain-based Service Network
owner: State Information Center (National Information Center), China Mobile, China UnionPay
public_harm_addressed: fragmented or untrusted blockchain identity infrastructure
adoption_penetration: Over 120 city nodes deployed within China, with BSN Spartan (international) nodes established in 20+ countries by early 2025, per CSIS analysis. [https://www.csis.org/blogs/strategic-technologies-blog/chinas-blockchain-playbook-infrastructure-influence-and-new]
source_note: CoinDesk confirms BSN is operated by China's National Information Center together with China Mobile and China UnionPay and hosts the RealDID national real-name DID system; commercial launch year not confirmed from source. [Batch year-fill: 2020 (official commercial launch (entered into force)), high confidence. https://digichina.stanford.edu/work/knowledge-base-blockchain-based-service-network-bsn-区块链服务网络]

name: Identitas Kependudukan Digital (Digital Population Identity)
owner: Directorate General of Population & Civil Registration (Ditjen Dukcapil), Ministry of Home Affairs (Kemendagri)
owner_normalised: Directorate General of Population & Civil Registration
public_harm_addressed: ID fraud, physical-card forgery, service exclusion
references_builds_on: Population Administration Law (UU Adminduk); Permendagri No. 72/2022
adoption_penetration: Over 14 million users had installed/used the IKD app, with 244,289 citizens completing remote identity verification, as of 26 Feb 2025 (World Bank project document); government target is 25 million citizens installed-and-authenticated by December 2027. [https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099040125074024669/text/P175218-d03fd493-98b8-4e10-9c27-499c7c04f5e6.txt]
source_note: Indonesia's official regulation portal confirms Minister of Home Affairs Regulation (Permendagri) No. 72 of 2022 governs e-KTP hardware/software/blank specifications and the operation of Identitas Kependudukan Digital (IKD).

name: National Digital ID Platform
owner: National Digital ID Co., Ltd. (licensed by ETDA)
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud in online onboarding, personal-data over-sharing
references_builds_on: ETDA Digital ID framework; ISO/IEC 29115 identity assurance levels
adoption_penetration: More than 60 million usable digital identities and 30+ million registered user accounts on the NDID platform, with 180+ member organizations (banks, telcos, government agencies, regulators) as of Jan 2026 and roughly 2 million transactions/month, per NDID's own reporting (May 2026). [https://ndid.co.th/en/ndid-sixty-million-identities-one-trust-framework-2/]
source_note: NDID site confirms an IdP/RP/AS/Proxy federated model providing eKYC/eConsent/eSignature; holds ETDA's Digital Identity Exchange Service License and ISO 27001:2022; exact launch year not stated on source. [Batch year-fill: 2018 (founded/established), high confidence. https://ndid.co.th/en/ndid-sixty-million-identities-one-trust-framework-2/]

name: ThaID
owner: Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA), Bureau of Registration Administration, Ministry of Interior
public_harm_addressed: impersonation, identity fraud
references_builds_on: DOPA registration administration / national Digital ID framework
adoption_penetration: Over 28 million Thai citizens registered/verified through ThaID as of 27 Oct 2025, with 400,000+ citizens using the online house-registration transfer service in the app's first year, per Thai media citing the Department of Provincial Administration. [https://www.posttoday.com/smart-city/732445]
source_note: DOPA/BORA official page (dated 14 Mar 2023) confirms ThaID is the government Digital ID app with face verification, operated by the Department of Provincial Administration.

name: Philippine Identification System
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud, exclusion of unbanked/undocumented
references_builds_on: Republic Act No. 11055 (2018); Implementing Rules & Regulations 2018
adoption_penetration: 90,582,172 Filipinos registered and verified as of 30 Nov 2025 (55M+ physical cards distributed, 89M+ digital IDs via eGovPH); 56,520,952 National ID authentications recorded as of 17 Sept 2025, per the Philippine Statistics Authority. [https://philsys.gov.ph/56m-national-id-authentications-largest-use-cases-in-social-protection-financial-inclusion/]
effectiveness_verified: Reduced-harm: DSWD used PhilSys to clean its Listahanan poverty-targeting database, removing duplicate/fraudulent beneficiary records, and Asia United Bank cut mobile-wallet account approval time from 2-3 days to 1 day using PhilSys authentication. [https://philsys.gov.ph/56m-national-id-authentications-largest-use-cases-in-social-protection-financial-inclusion/]
source_note: PhilSys official site confirms the system was established by RA No. 11055 (signed Aug 2018, IRR approved Oct 2018), implemented by the PSA, with PhilID/ePhilID/digital national ID components; registration began 2020.

name: Singpass / National Digital Identity
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud, phishing, transaction repudiation
adoption_penetration: Over 4.5 million users, covering 97% of Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents aged 15+; 700+ organizations offering 2,000+ services; 350+ million transactions/year (Ministry of Digital Development and Information factsheet, Feb 2022). [https://www.mddi.gov.sg/newsroom/singpass-factsheet-02032022/]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — Myinfo data-prefill cut average application time by up to 80% and lifted business approval rates by up to 15% via improved data quality; Face Verification cut password-reset time from ~10 minutes to seconds (GovTech/MDDI factsheet). [https://www.mddi.gov.sg/newsroom/singpass-factsheet-02032022/]
source_note: Singpass official site confirms it is Singapore residents' trusted national digital identity spanning 700+ agencies/services with Myinfo and digital document signing; NDI is a Smart Nation strategic project (GovTech per MDDI factsheet; founding year not stated on source). [Batch year-fill: 2003 (Singpass (predecessor of the National Digital Identity/NDI initiative) was launched/adopted as Singapore's national digital identity credential system), high confidence. https://www.imda.gov.sg/-/media/imda/files/inner/archive/news-and-events/news_and_events_level2/20071105103244/singpass5nov07annexa.pdf]

name: My Number (Individual Number) System & My Number Card
owner: Digital Agency and J-LIS (Japan Agency for Local Authority Information Systems)
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud, administrative record mismatch
references_builds_on: My Number Act (Act on Use of Numbers to Identify Specific Individuals)
adoption_penetration: Approximately 97.99 million cards possessed as of end-April 2025, equal to 78.5% of Japan's population (up from 35.9M/28.7% in Mar 2021 and 84.4M/67.6% in Mar 2023) — Japan Digital Agency. [https://www.digital.go.jp/assets/contents/node/basic_page/field_ref_resources/851e38fd-7aa6-474b-ac14-14d9fedd695e/d5ad3c36/20250519_meeting_mynumber_card_mynumber_outline_05.pdf]
source_note: Digital Agency site confirms My Number identifies individuals in administrative procedures and is operated by the Digital Agency; individual numbers were assigned to all residents from Oct 2015 (per HRC Japan). [Validation: bindingness 'mandatory' applies to Individual Number assignment (compulsory under the My Number Act); My Number Card issuance itself is voluntary.]

name: Japanese Public Key Infrastructure
owner: J-LIS (Japan Agency for Local Authority Information Systems)
public_harm_addressed: online impersonation, document tampering and repudiation
adoption_penetration: Approximately 1,246 private companies were using JPKI (e.g., for bank account opening, securities transactions, loan signing) as of April 30, 2026 — Japan Digital Agency. [https://www.digital.go.jp/en/policies/mynumber/private-business/jpki-introduction]
source_note: Digital Agency site confirms JPKI is operated by J-LIS as trust anchor; the My Number Card holds a user-authentication certificate and a digital-signature certificate for online authentication and tamper-proof signatures. [Batch year-fill: 2004 (entered into force / service launched), high confidence. https://www.mhlw.go.jp/shingi/2009/02/dl/s0206-7d_0001.pdf]

name: VNeID
owner: Ministry of Public Security (Department C06), Vietnam
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud, impersonation
adoption_penetration: Over 102.1 million electronic identity profiles created and 71.5 million accounts activated, as reported July 2, 2026 by Báo Công An Nhân Dân (the Ministry of Public Security's official newspaper). [https://baomoi.com/vneid-dat-hon-102-trieu-ho-so-dinh-danh-kich-hoat-71-5-trieu-tai-khoan-c55531112.epi]

name: Fayda National ID (National ID Program)
owner: National ID Program (NIDP), Government of Ethiopia
public_harm_addressed: identity exclusion from financial/telecom/government services
references_builds_on: Built on MOSIP (Modular Open Source Identity Platform), an open-source digital public good; Ethiopia/IIIT-Bangalore partnership with MOSIP began June 2020, later branded 'Fayda'.
adoption_penetration: 37.5 million people enrolled as of March 10, 2026 (about 1 million new registrants/week), per National ID Office Executive Director Yodahe Arayaselassie; program targets 90 million registrations by June 2026 (originally 70 million by end-2025). [https://newbusinessethiopia.com/technology/ethiopia-national-digital-id-users-surpass-37-million/]

name: National Identification Number / National Identity Management Commission
public_harm_addressed: identity fraud; exclusion from services and rights
adoption_penetration: 136 million NINs registered as of ~July 2026 (up from 123.9 million in October 2025), per NIMC Director-General Abisoye Coker-Odusote; official target is 180 million by December 2026. public_harm_addressed: identity fraud; exclusion; data-protection risk

[https://idtechwire.com/judge-halts-kenyas-digital-id-effort-citing-constitutional-concerns/]

name: EMV Integrated Circuit Card Specifications for Payment Systems (Contact Chip, Books 1-4)
public_harm_addressed: counterfeit-card and chip payment fraud
adoption_penetration: 97% of card-present transactions worldwide were EMV chip transactions as of Q4 2025 (EMVCo, aggregating American Express, Discover, JCB, Mastercard, UnionPay, Visa data). [https://www.emvco.com/about-us/worldwide-emv-deployment-statistics/ ; https://www.kansascityfed.org/research/payments-system-research-briefings/did-card-present-fraud-rates-decline-in-the-united-states-after-the-migration-to-chip-cards/]
effectiveness_verified: mixed — Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City research briefing on the US chip migration: on dual-message networks (Visa/Mastercard/Discover credit and signature-debit), counterfeit card-present fraud did not decline (9.0 to 9.1 basis points, 2015-2021) and lost-or-stolen fraud nearly tripled (1.6 to 4.5 bps), with overall card-present fraud rising (10.1 to 14.9 bps, 2017-2021); by contrast, single-message PIN-debit networks (STAR/NYCE/Pulse) saw counterfeit fraud fall (3.2 to 1.7 bps) and overall card-present fraud decline (6.5 to 3.7 bps). [https://www.emvco.com/about-us/worldwide-emv-deployment-statistics/ ; https://www.kansascityfed.org/research/payments-system-research-briefings/did-card-present-fraud-rates-decline-in-the-united-states-after-the-migration-to-chip-cards/]
source_note: EMVCo page confirms EMVCo owns/maintains the EMV Chip (contact) Specifications; specific version/year not stated on page, left blank. [Batch year-fill: 1996 (first published / adopted - original EMV '96 Integrated Circuit Card Specification for Payment Systems (Version 3.0), dated June 30, 1996, jointly copyrighted by Europay, MasterCard, and Visa; this is the direct predecessor to today's EMV Contact Chip Books 1-4 maintained by EMVCo (formed 1999)), high confidence. http://www.ttfn.net/techno/smartcards/cardspec.pdf]

name: EMV Contactless Specifications for Payment Systems (Books A-D)
public_harm_addressed: contactless/NFC card fraud and interoperability failure
references_builds_on: EMV Contact ICC Specifications; ISO/IEC 14443 (contactless interface)
adoption_penetration: UK Finance's 2025 Annual Fraud Report states 74% of all UK card transactions were contactless in 2024. [https://www.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2025-05/UK%20Finance%20Annual%20Fraud%20report%202025.pdf]
effectiveness_verified: reduced-harm — UK Finance (2025) found contactless fraud was only 7% of overall card fraud losses despite being 74% of transactions; the contactless fraud-to-turnover ratio was 1.3p per £100 vs 6.0p for card fraud overall, and 2024 (£41.1m) was the first year-on-year decline in contactless fraud losses since 2020. [https://www.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2025-05/UK%20Finance%20Annual%20Fraud%20report%202025.pdf]
source_note: EMVCo page confirms EMVCo as owner and lists current Contactless Books (A/B/C-2/C-7/C-8) at v2.12 dated 6 Jul 2026.

name: BGP Prefix Origin Validation (RPKI-based Route Origin Validation)
